item.title: She blocked his bid to become a federal judge. Now he's running for her Senate seat.
item.description:
Why are major Democrats and Republicans flocking to Mississippi in recent weeks?

In a climate where polls show President Donald Trump's approval ratings cratering, Democrats are unusually optimistic about Scott Colom's chances of flipping the Senate seat held by incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith -- even in deep-red Mississippi.

"We got to have a senator that looks out for Mississippi, that puts Mississippi farmers first, Mississippi small businesses first, represent our values by not allowing corruption to ruin our country and actually delivers on the commitments to put America first," Colom told ABC News in an interview earlier this week.

The incumbent's campaign dismisses the Democratic push as the last-ditch effort of a campaign that will fall short.

Gov. Wes Moore says key races in South 'in play,' Democrats 'made mistakes' not investing earlier

Colom is a district attorney for four counties along the Mississippi-Alabama border and a former nominee to become a U.S. district judge. He would be Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

Democrats have argued that Colom's prominent credentials, as well as voter pushback against Republican incumbents and motivation among Democratic-leaning Black voters, could help boost him. Mississippi's population is around 36% Black, according to U.S. Census data.

Colom faces an uphill battle, as Mississippi has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1982 and voted for Donald Trump in 2024 by around 20 points. ABC News rates the race solid Republican.

But he has gotten the attention of national Democrats; major party figures such as former former Vice President Kamala Harris and Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock have campaigned with him. Former President Barack Obama also recorded an ad for him released earlier this month.

Harris, during a rally with Colom on Thursday, told attendees, "I've been in those rooms where there's no cameras, it's senators talking to each other... When you have a voice like his in that room, just think about the impact that's going to have on the decisions coming out of that room. Think about that. This is no ordinary time, and this is no ordinary man."

Colom also went viral online last week after a social video he posted showed Hyde-Smith, during a local news interview from February, saying "You have so many proteins to choose from" while discussing how to deal with higher prices on meat and other goods. In the interview, Hyde-Smith also spoke about working on regulations that would help energy production, and tax incentives to help development.

But it was the proteins part that Colom's campaign seized on, with a punchy video that featured voters mocking the senator's words, with one saying, "Pick another protein ... I'd rather pick another Senator instead." (The campaign has confirmed to ABC News that the video has been turned into a campaign ad.)

One concrete sign of confidence among Democrats over Colom's chances came on Tuesday, when the Senate Majority PAC, an outside group aligned with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, announced it would spend $1.2 million on an ad campaign across broadcast TV and digital for ads for Colom.

Asked what signs the group sees in Mississippi that makes it worth investing in, spokesperson Lauren French wrote, "Cindy Hyde-Smith has spent a decade in Washington without passing a single piece of legislation, and Mississippians have noticed."

Hyde-Smith has cosponsored legislation that has passed into law but legislation she initially sponsored or reintroduced has not become law, according to congressional records. Asked to respond to Senate Majority PAC, Hyde-Smith's campaign pointed to how bills from lawmakers "are often passed as part of larger legislative packages," and that has been true for some of Hyde-Smith's bills, including the first one she introduced. The campaign also pointed out that she is running for only her second full term.

French said Colom is running a "disciplined campaign" with messages resonating with voters.

Colom and Hyde-Smith have some history, as she blocked his nomination for federal judge in 2023. She cited his support for transgender rights and having previously been boosted by a George Soros-linked PAC, according to the Mississippi Free Press.

He insists his bid for Senate is not motivated by a desire to get back at her.

"It has nothing to do with the run for me ... as a Christian, I forgive her. It's about the people in Mississippi," Colom told ABC News.

Hyde-Smith dismissed Colom's chances.

"We are confident that Mississippians will once again send Cindy Hyde-Smith back to the U.S. Senate on November 3rd. This is simply Washington insiders making a last ditch effort to give life to Scott Colom's failing campaign," campaign manager Jake Monssen told ABC News in a statement.

Hyde-Smith's supporters may be more motivated after a boost from President Donald Trump, who's set to hold a rally in Mississippi on Monday as part of a swing of campaign rallies mostly in red states.

The Republican National Committee announced the rally around a week after Colom's social video went viral, although Trump and the group have not indicated why they are doing the rally there and Trump has expressed confidence in Hyde-Smith.

"Cindy Hyde-Smith's very popular ... So if I need to get her over the top, I would go there [to Mississippi]. She's great. Cindy Hyde-Smith is great," Trump told reporters when asked Thursday about the Senate election.

Hyde-Smith will be attending the rally, according to her campaign.

This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/Politics/democrats-aim-deep-red-mississippi-senate-seat-scott/story?id=137484924

item.title: 县委书记回应被扔下水：张雪临时起意
item.description:
澎湃新闻 综合报道
10月25日，张雪机车创始人张雪在家乡湖南麻阳，驾驶改装摩托车MX450，用时32分钟，成功刷新“改装摩托车在开阔水域行驶最远距离”吉尼斯世界纪录。
据九派新闻报道，庆祝时麻阳县委书记廖园熙被众人抬着扔进水里，其称是张雪临时提议还问自己会不会游泳，“幸好会游泳”，觉得很有意思。
廖园熙表示，挺开心的，县里全力配合这次挑战活动，张雪团队也非常努力，他相信这个好结果预示着张雪机车会越来越好，麻阳以后也会越来越好。

17年前，张雪曾4次驾驶摩托车挑战“水上漂”，连人带车摔进水里，遗憾失利。张雪表示，今天在故乡圆梦，也是想让这片土地被世界看见。

澎湃新闻此前报道，1987年，张雪出生于湖南怀化麻阳的一个贫困山村。少年时代的他对摩托车有着近乎偏执的热爱，却因家境贫寒只能选择“曲线救国”：16岁初中毕业，他便进入摩托车修理店当学徒，白天拆修车辆、钻研机械原理，晚上抱着发动机研究到深夜；17岁时，他用攒下的微薄积蓄开了自己的修车行，正式踏入摩托车行业。


2006年，19岁的张雪为了争取职业赛车手的机会，骑着一辆车龄比自己还大的二手摩托车，冒雨在泥泞山路上追逐湖南卫视《晚间》节目组一百多公里。他浑身湿透、多次摔车却始终不肯放弃，最终用这份执着打动了节目组，获得了宝贵的拍摄机会，也由此正式踏入职业赛车领域。


此后数年，张雪辗转多地，当过全职赛车手，也在摩托车工厂担任过技术岗位。正是这段从赛场到工厂的经历，让他完整吃透了整车研发的全流程。从维修、改装到制造的一线经验，在他心中埋下了一颗种子：造中国人自己的高性能摩托车。


此前报道：张雪提议插播家乡广告，县委书记“拒绝”了


（综合 刘蓓/九派新闻、新华社、岳怀让/澎湃新闻）

item.title: 李天阳不敌张本智和摘银，陈熠夺得女单冠军，国乒亚锦赛4金收官
item.description:
澎湃新闻记者 祁东

北京时间10月25日，2026年乒乓球亚锦赛在乌兹别克斯坦迎来最后一个比赛日的争夺。

在最后一个项目——男单项目的决赛中，国乒选手李天阳与日本选手张本智和交锋，最终以11比1、11比9、7比11、8比11、7比11告负。

此前在半决赛中，李天阳以3比2逆转中国台北队选手郭冠宏晋级。来到决赛舞台，他迎来了自己与张本智和的首次交锋。最终，李天阳遗憾与金牌擦肩而过。

而在当天稍早前结束的女单决赛中，国乒选手陈熠对阵日本选手张本美和，最终陈熠气势如虹，以11比5、11比8、11比6连赢三局，赢得本届赛事女单冠军。

陈熠 资料图

此前在半决赛中，陈熠击败王艺迪晋级决赛，张本美和则是半决赛战胜蒯曼过关。来到决赛，陈熠展现出了良好的竞技状态。

陈熠与张本美和此前曾交手14次，两人各胜7场。但在2022年以来的8次交锋中，陈熠只取得一场胜利，且已吞下4连败，包括本届亚锦赛女团决赛以0比3告负。不过如今来到女单决赛，陈熠实现了复仇。

由此，国乒在本届亚锦赛以4金收官，收获了男子团体、男子双打、女子双打、女子单打这4个项目的金牌，在女子团体、混合双打、男子单打则收获银牌。


本期编辑 徐滁

item.title: 特朗普：把白宫记者团搬到一个“不那么招人烦的地方”
item.description:
当地时间10月24日，美国总统特朗普在社交媒体平台上驳斥了有关他打算拆除白宫新闻简报室、恢复其正下方旧泳池的报道，但同时表示，他可能会把白宫记者团迁到一个“不那么招人烦的地方”。


据美国《纽约时报》20日报道，特朗普已向身边助手提出，希望拆除白宫新闻简报室，恢复位于其正下方的旧泳池。这座泳池建于1933年，是时任总统富兰克林·罗斯福为治疗小儿麻痹症后遗症而修建的。上世纪70年代尼克松政府时期，泳池被改建为新闻简报室，即现在的詹姆斯·布雷迪厅。


特朗普24日在社交媒体平台“真实社交”上写道：“有一则假新闻报道，说我打算拆除白宫新闻简报室，把埋在它正下方的旧泳池恢复原样。”他接着写道：“虽然我有可能把这些假新闻媒体迁到一个不那么招人烦的地方，但旧泳池永远不会复原。我压根儿就没想过要做这么蠢的事！”


《纽约时报》的报道还称，按这一设想，白宫记者团将被迁往街对面的艾森豪威尔行政办公大楼。该方案已得到特朗普身边一些顾问的支持。白宫通讯主任史蒂文·张就此表示，“所有选项都还在桌面上”，相关决定将在适当时候宣布。


美国《国会山报》24日报道称，本周，白宫将英国《独立报》记者安德鲁·费因伯格从总统随行报道团中除名，禁止他登上空军一号随总统出行。就在此前一天，特朗普刚在椭圆形办公室严厉斥责过这名记者。白宫一名发言人日前向《国会山报》回应称：“任何人、任何记者，都没有宪法赋予的权利，可以随意进入总统的椭圆形办公室、空军一号专机或是其他敏感、私密场所。一旦媒体刊发不实报道、捏造事实、罔顾真相，他们也就没必要近距离采访了，大可以在安保区域之外杜撰报道。”


就在上个月，白宫记者协会还谴责了特朗普政府禁止《政客》、美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）以及MS NOW（原微软全国广播公司）进入白宫采访的决定。该禁令引发广泛批评，一名联邦法官随后下令恢复上述媒体的采访权限。不过，和费因伯格一样，CNN记者至今仍不能登上空军一号、加入总统随行报道团。



环球时报记者 杜天琦

item.title: 卫生间的“它”，竟然烧了家！速查家中这类“神器”
item.description:
近日 贵州省贵阳市云岩区

一高层居民楼发生火情


△图源：贵州消防


消防员接到报警后

迅速赶往现场

发现起火点为

卫生间内的智能马桶

随即快速将火扑灭


△图源：贵州消防


经初步调查

火灾疑似由

智能马桶线路短路引发


△图源：贵州消防


随着科技的发展

一些智能家电

极大解放了我们的双手

方便了日常生活

但背后隐藏的火灾隐患

也不容忽视

警惕智能家电“惹火”


  • 2026年3月，江苏常州一居民家中的智能马桶在使用过程中突然冒烟起火，户主立即切断电源，并拨打了119报警电话。

  • 2026年1月，江苏省泰州市海陵区，一栋三层民房深夜起火，起火原因为电动窗帘线路发生故障，局部过热引燃周边可燃物。‌

△图源：贵州消防


  • 2025年3月，河北唐山方先生家中的充电餐桌突冒火花，直冲屋顶。该充电餐桌于6、7年前购入，价格约3万元，起火疑因内部电池发生故障所致。

  • 2024年12月，贵州贵阳一小区居民家智能门锁因锂电池故障发生自燃，火苗蔓延引燃周围可燃物。

△图源：贵州消防

智能家电为何会“发火”？


这些技术先进、功能强大的智能电器，为什么会“惹火”？


选了“不定时炸弹”


  • 购买了“三无”产品，安全系数极低。

  • 部分厂家为压缩成本，使用劣质电线、电子元件等，容易出现短路、漏电等问题。


使用时的“坏习惯”


  • 电器通电后无人看管，长时间处于充电状态。

  • 电器持续运行，长期不间断工作。

  • 多个电器设备共用插座或长时间运行，超出负荷，引发线路过热。

  • 智能马桶、电动泡脚桶等在潮湿环境中工作，易发生漏电或短路。


“年久失修”埋隐患


  • 未定期清理滤网、散热孔等，被灰尘、杂物堵塞。

  • 电器长时间使用后，内部线路绝缘层可能破损、老化，未能及时更换。

家电起火 牢记三步


  • 先断电。

    第一时间切断总电源！

  • 再覆盖。

    确保断电后，应用干粉或二氧化碳灭火器扑救。切记不要用水浇！


  • 速撤离。

    若火势已大，无法控制，应立即放弃扑救，迅速撤离现场并拨打119火警电话。

省心的智能生活

离不开用心的安全守护

日常应及时维修更换老化电器

如发生电气火灾

立即切断电源 移开周围物品

用干粉或二氧化碳灭火器扑救

切记不可用水灭火

item.title: Poll finds Democrats still boosted by voters' economic concerns
item.description:
Call it the "avoidance" election, with many on each side more motivated by trying to prevent or stop things than by what they'll gain.

Against a backdrop of continued concern about inflation and the economy, Democrats maintain their lead in a bid for a House majority. They're currently on pace for 229 seats in our CBS News House model estimate, which translates voters' congressional preferences into seats. 

The potential range of outcomes could reach into the 230s in our model, but Republicans do still have a very narrow path to hold the majority, too.

While that Democratic lead has been durable over recent weeks, it hasn't expanded, either. 

In other words, there isn't a growing wave, at least not as of today. 

If anything, the still undecided or uncertain voters tend to profile as more Republican. 

Whether they decide to show up is perhaps the key question of 2026.

Either way, voters describe a dynamic in which they're more motivated in opposition to things they think might happen. For instance:

More think gas prices will go up if Republicans win than if Democrats do.

(Though they don't think Democrats will make gas prices go down.)

Most voters don't think Democrats have a plan and won't make people financially better off, either...But more voters think they'll be worse off if Republicans win.

The president remains a central factor. It would be a high number voting either to support or oppose a president in a midterm if this sentiment holds through Election Day. 

Most of the Democrats' voters are trying to oppose either President Trump or Republicans, even more than to help Democrats. 

(Whether that rationale ultimately limits Democrats' gains or not is another key question.)

But he's motivating for most Republicans, especially MAGA.

Some of this lead is attributed to more Democrats saying they'll either definitely vote, or have already voted early.

But this is not over: The voters who describe themselves as only "probably" or "maybe" going to vote are more Republican. If they become motivated, this can all change.

So, what happens if either party wins?

Few voters think gas prices will go down no matter who wins. 

But the GOP is now relatively more associated in voters' minds with rising gas prices: More think they'll go up if Republicans win than if Democrats do.

Most voters don't think they'll be better off financially, no matter who wins. That cynicism does permeate the electorate. 

But as a choice, relatively more think they'll do better with Democrats.

Most voters think there will be more corruption in government if Republicans maintain control of Congress.

Both Democrats and Republicans — at about similar large majorities — see government corruption as a factor in their votes.

The Trump factor: A motivator for both sides, but more so for Democrats

Mr. Trump looms large over the midterms, particularly for Democrats. More than seven in 10 voting for Democrats say their vote for Congress is to oppose him. 

Mr. Trump is also a factor for those backing Republicans. Most say their vote is to support him, but to a lesser extent than Democrats are voting to oppose him.   

For most who are backing Democrats, their motivation is more about stopping Mr. Trump and GOP policies than advancing the Democrats' own policies. 

Here's how prevalent opposition to either party is as a motivating force this year.

Neither Democrats nor Republicans are perceived by a majority of voters as having a clear plan, should either win control of Congress.

There are four in 10 voters supporting Democrats who don't believe the party has a clear plan, should they win. They say opposition to Mr. Trump is the main motivator for them. 

Meanwhile, there are four in 10 voting Republican who say their vote isn't about the president. They're less likely to consider themselves MAGA, tend to just "somewhat," rather than "strongly," approve of Mr. Trump. But a big majority of them have an unfavorable view of the Democratic Party – so they remain in the Republican camp.

Other issues

Many voters feel a win by the other side is a threat to their way of life. Democrats think a Republican win would be a threat to theirs.

MAGA Republicans in particular, more so than non-MAGA, think the Democrats would be a threat. 

Although the issue ranks behind others as a factor in voters' decisions, Republicans lead Democrats among those who consider transgender issues a major factor in their vote.

Immigration

There are a third of voters who think the Democratic Party puts the interests of recent immigrants ahead of those of U.S. citizens, and voters who hold this view are backing Republicans in big numbers.

(Another third does think the Democratic Party prioritizes both groups, and these voters are supporting Democrats.)

Trump and finances

Americans' overall ratings of the economy continue to be negative, as they have been for years. They've even dipped a bit lower now, to where they were last spring.

And most likely voters feel the president's policies are making them financially worse off.

The economy and inflation remain top concerns. Those calling inflation a very important issue mostly back Democrats, as do those who feel prices have been difficult or a hardship.

Against that backdrop, voters voice broader concern about whose financial interests they think the president prioritizes.

More feel he prioritizes his own financial interests and those of his family over the financial interests of the people in the country. And those who hold this view are backing Democrats.

Republicans mostly feel Mr. Trump prioritizes the financial interests of people in the country over his own.

Trump on the trail: Is he helping or hurting?

The president's numerous appearances on the campaign trail may help to rally the base behind Republican candidates, but those events may not have as much impact with the rest of the party. 

Most MAGA Republicans say that when they see Trump campaigning for political candidates, it makes them more likely to vote for Republicans. 

For many non-MAGA Republicans, these campaign events do not do that.

The voting process

Most voters express at least some confidence in their own local and county elections administration to conduct the election process, including determining eligibility and correctly counting ballots. 

In turn, most tend to voice confidence that their own vote will be recorded and counted accurately in this election. 

On both of these measures, more Democrats than Republicans are very confident.

Republicans are far more likely to believe that illegal voting by non-citizens happens in federal elections. 

This CBS News/YouGov survey was conducted with a nationally representative sample of 2,355 U.S. adults interviewed between October 21-23, 2026. The sample was weighted to be representative of adults nationwide according to gender, age, race, and education, based on the U.S. Census American Community Survey and Current Population Survey, as well as 2024 presidential vote. The margin of error for the total sample is ±2.6 points, it is ± 2.9  points for the sample of registered voters, and  ± 3.0 points for likely voters.

The estimated numbers of Republican and Democratic seats come from a statistical model developed by CBS News and YouGov which includes data from this poll, past vote and other district-level characteristics, demographics and historical patterns. These estimates are subject to statistical error. We simulate many elections, with the error calibrated to include historical polling accuracy, to obtain a range of seat estimates. We report 95% confidence intervals from the simulations. These estimates describe which party is ahead today and may change as additional data are collected closer to the election.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/poll-house-estimate-midterm-elections-2026/

item.title: 大陆设“台湾光复纪念日”一周年 洪秀柱赴中谈“统一”
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/大陆设“台湾光复纪念日”一周年 洪秀柱赴中谈“统一”/a-79755791
item.description:
德正
2026-10-25T14:27:56.274Z
2025年5月，台湾立法院通过修法，将”台湾光复节“更名为“台湾光复暨金门古宁头大捷纪念日”

（德国之声中文网）据中国官媒新华社报道，本周日（10月25日）上午，福建省福州市举办纪念台湾光复81周年座谈会。报道称，台湾抗日遗属、在台牺牲的革命者后人、两岸青少年及港澳和海外代表，专家学者等赴会者共计约200人。

国民党前主席洪秀柱出席并发表讲话。据台湾《联合新闻网》报道，洪秀柱称日本在侵华失败后毫无反思与悔意，“仍然在妄图恢复军国主义，不能不严加防范此等狼子野心的复苏”。

洪秀柱强调不能一方面期待稳定，一方面不断煽动敌意，认为任由去中国化和外国势力发展，几十年后具有家国情怀的人将逐渐凋零，两岸青年将视彼此为陌路，甚至兵戎相见，“我们还有什么面目区间九泉之下的抗日先烈？”

洪秀柱还批评民进党，称其“为谋取一党一己之私，在台湾大搞去中国化，篡改历史教科书……抹去抗战与光复的血泪记忆，在孩子的心灵中植入仇恨与对立。”其认为“民族认同的混乱，正是当前台湾内部撕裂与两岸对立的根本危机。”

洪秀柱言论大陆捧 台媒批

据台湾《自由时报》报道，洪秀柱在座谈会上表示“如果再不携手谋求民族复兴，完成‘和平统一’大业，台湾的未来将不可想象。”并呼吁“期待广大台湾乡亲，特别是青年朋友，能够拨开迷雾勇敢找回‘堂堂正正中国人’的骄傲。”

洪秀柱在福州的发言被大陆媒体多方转载。

台湾《自由时报》采访熟稔统战的台湾官员，后者批评国民党迎合中共统一叙事，每次在重要节点，就会赴中唱和，呼应中共统战操作，称洪秀柱的言论“一点也不意外”。

中国官媒新华网则将洪秀柱的讲话概括报道为“期盼两岸同胞共同传承抗日先贤守护国土的精神，坚定朝和平统一的方向努力，为实现中华民族伟大复兴而努力奋斗。”

中国军媒批民进党“媚日”

1946年10月18日（民国35年）10月25日被确定为法定假日”台湾光复节“，为纪念1945年10月25日台湾受降。

1949年10月25日，中共军队在进攻金门的战役中大败，国民党赢得内战后期少有的一场大捷，史称”古宁头大捷“。

2025年5月，台湾立法院通过修法，将”台湾光复节“更名为“台湾光复暨金门古宁头大捷纪念日”。

2025年10月24日，中国全国人大常委会表决通过将10月25日设立为“台湾光复纪念日”。民进党当时发文表示，中共试图利用“台湾光复纪念日”来否定台湾的主权，并压缩台湾在国际舞台上的空间。赖清德则在脸书上发文纪念古宁头战役，“76年前，在金门的古宁头，爆发了扭转台湾历史的重要战役……挡下中共的入侵，塑造了数十年的和平”。

一年后的今天，中国解放军官媒“钧正平工作室”发文，强调“台湾光复历史不容篡改”，并批评赖清德“顽固走‘去中抗中’邪路”，称其“处心积虑构建‘媚日史观’‘台独史观’”，称其“将侵略者粉饰为台湾恩人”是“认贼作父、数典忘祖”的行为。

郑丽文吁铭记历史 避免战争

国民党现任主席郑丽文亦在脸书上发文纪念“台湾光复节”，她写道“殖民伤痕不应被美化，”“不该因为彼此的出身、认同或政治立场，就否定对这片土地的感情。”郑丽文表示“台湾的未来，需要安全，需要尊严，也需要和平，”要“有面对风险的准备，更要有避免战争的决心”。

中国发布卫星俯瞰台湾影像

中国官媒央视新闻在本周日发布名为“吉林一号卫星太空视角俯瞰我国宝岛台湾”的影像，称”每条街道都清晰可见“。影片长42秒，从中正纪念堂到台北故宫博物院，再到台北大巨蛋，孙中山纪念馆，中正桥，玉山山脉、日月潭、淡水河、花莲清水断崖、宜兰壮围乡、台南青鲲鯓扇形盐田、嘉义湿地及台北港景观均有呈现。

item.title: 分析揭示 流行歌曲越来越冷漠了
item.description:
来源: 
煎蛋

密歇根州立大学研究发现，从1947年到2024年的流行歌词中，情感与社交表达持续减少，焦虑词汇增加而悲伤词汇减少。

我们在听流行音乐时，常常会被其中的歌词打动。然而，来自密歇根州立大学心理学系的一项最新研究却揭示了一个意想不到的现象：在过去几十年的流行音乐中，歌词里的情感和人际关系表达正在逐年减少。无论对比不同时代的音乐人，还是观察同一位音乐人一生的创作历程，这种情感淡化的趋势都清晰可见。

这项发表在《美学、创造力与艺术心理学》期刊上的研究，是迄今为止针对流行歌词规模最大的分析。研究团队搜集了从1947年到2024年间近一个世纪的流行音乐数据，涵盖230位音乐人的38467首歌曲。为了确保数据的准确性，大约30名研究助理对每位音乐人的作品目录进行了人工核对。

研究发现，随着时间的推移，歌词中涉及正面情绪和负面情绪的词汇都在减少，对家庭和朋友等社交关系的提及也日益稀少。如果细分具体的情绪类型，与焦虑相关的词汇显著增加，而表达悲伤的词汇则有所下降。研究联合作者、心理学副教授Jan Brascamp指出，过往研究多侧重于探讨不同年代音乐之间的宏观差异，而这项研究同时观察了音乐人个人职业生涯的变化，从而能够将艺术家自身的转变与音乐产业及社会文化的宏观变迁区分开来。总体而言，不同时代音乐人之间的群体差异，要大于单个音乐人一生中的变化。

研究涉及的230位音乐人风格各异。其中Willie Nelson贡献了数量最多的歌词作品，而Miles Davis有歌词的作品数量最少。像Marvin Gaye和The Supremes这样的经典灵魂乐与早期摇滚音乐人，其歌词在正面情感和社交联系上的得分最高。相比之下，像Nine Inch Nails和Sex Pistols等反主流文化流派的音乐人，得分则处于较低水平。此外，负面情绪与悲伤表达在Hank Williams和Patsy Cline等老牌乡村与蓝调歌手的作品中占有极高的比例。

令人吃惊的是，歌词情感的变化轨迹并没有遵循人类心理衰老的常规规律。在日常生活中，随着年龄增长，人们通常会更擅长调节自身情绪，并更加珍视深厚的人际关系。如果歌词单纯反映个人心理成熟度，那么音乐人在职业生涯后期的作品应该包含更多正面情感与亲密关系。然而，数据呈现出的却是相反结果。研究第一作者Logan Gibson认为，这表明歌词的演变并非主要由个人的心理成熟驱动，而是受到艺术潮流、文化风向以及音乐工业力量的深远影响。

音乐绝不仅仅是娱乐工具。人们借由歌曲调节情绪、认识自我、塑造身份认同，并在聆听中寻求与他人的共鸣。研究联合作者William Chopik表示，歌词是记录艺术家乃至整个社会文化关注焦点的生动载体。当歌词中的情感与社交语言出现大规模退潮时，它引发了一个深层的思考：我们人类在现实生活中表达情感与维系关系的方式，是否也在经历着一场悄无声息的转变？

原文

关键词: 
流行歌曲
心理
娱乐
栏目: 
品味生活
作者: 
sein

item.title: 勒庞启动总统竞选 左翼奥尔良集会抗议
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

法国国民联盟领导人玛丽娜·勒庞10月25日在奥尔良举行大型集会，正式为2027年总统大选造势。勒庞表示，希望在当前社会和经济紧张背景下向法国“注入乐观”，并强调“复兴”而非进一步激化政治语气。

勒庞目前在多项总统选举民调中处于领先位置，国民联盟则继续以治安、移民控制、驱逐非法移民以及强化法国国家主权作为主要竞选议题。部分政策还涉及通过公投推动制度改革，并可能进一步挑战欧盟现行政策框架。

在勒庞集会前一天，奥尔良举行大规模反国民联盟示威。当地政府估计约1.3万人参加，主办方称人数达到2.6万；约3000名警察和宪兵被部署维持秩序。示威总体平静，但现场也显示法国左翼内部仍存在明显分歧。

距离法国总统大选约六个月，勒庞正试图进一步塑造能够执政的形象，而中间派和左翼阵营能否整合，也将成为选战的重要变量。

item.title: Trump says he's weighing deal with Iran against action to 'finish them off'
item.description:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump said it’s “getting to be decision time” on whether he will make a deal with Tehran or resume attacks as Iranian and Houthi threats against Americans in the Middle East continue to grow.

Most Read from Bloomberg

  • Trump Prepares for Iran Escalation After US, Israeli Polls
  • Bitcoin Billionaires Are Racing to Ride a 3,000% Crypto Boom
  • Amazon’s New Tablet Is a Credible iPad Rival for Much Less Money
  • Secretive Ukrainian Deep-Strike Unit Behind Rapid Expansion of Deep-Strike Campaign
  • Indonesia Begins Trimming Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore

“I have a decision to make: Do I finish it off, which would be very easy to do, or do I make a deal? That’s all,” Trump said in an interview with Fox News’ Sunday Morning Futures. “We don’t play games.”

Trump has suggested that US strikes on Iran could resume after the Nov. 3 midterm elections and he has sent additional forces, including a third aircraft carrier group, toward the Persian Gulf.

Officials warn the period between the election and the new Congress taking office could be particularly dangerous, with a negotiated deal seen as the most likely way to end the conflict.

The US is reducing diplomatic and military staffing in parts of the Middle East amid growing threats from Iran and the Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen. 

The State Department had initially acknowledged departures only from Saudi Arabia, but an American official told Bloomberg News Friday that staffing changes are taking place more broadly as Iran intensifies attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: 巴西总统决选投票 弗拉维奥·博索纳罗民调51%领先卢拉
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

巴西10月25日举行总统选举第二轮投票，现任总统卢拉与右翼参议员弗拉维奥·博索纳罗展开最后对决。最新Datafolha民调显示，按有效票计算，弗拉维奥支持率为51%，卢拉49%，两个百分点差距仍处于误差范围内，选情高度胶着。

本月第一轮投票中，弗拉维奥获得约47.0%，卢拉约45.2%，前者领先超过200万票。

81岁的卢拉争取第四个总统任期，主打社会福利、民主制度以及抵御美国贸易压力；45岁的弗拉维奥则强调打击犯罪、削减公共开支和更保守的社会政策。两人在选前辩论中围绕经济、治安、医疗、腐败及对美关系激烈交锋。

巴西约1.6亿选民有资格投票。此次决选不仅决定巴西未来四年的经济和社会政策方向，也被视为拉美左、右翼力量消长的重要观察指标。

关键词: 
巴西

item.title: 日本网络攻击激增 自民党促设首相主导应对机制
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

日本近期网络攻击和信息泄露事件明显增加，自民党10月23日向首相高市早苗提交建议，将当前形势形容为“网络紧急事态前夜”，要求由首相官邸主导设立“网络应对本部”，统一协调政府部门和民间机构的防御工作。

Recorded Future最新报告显示，2026年第三季度与日本有关的网络攻击报告达到918起，较第二季度的621起增加48%，受影响行业包括零售、铁路、物流、媒体、教育和软件等。

日本企业和政府近期接连发生资料泄露及系统遭非法访问事件。NHK出版相关服务约12.7万条用户资料泄露，数字厅也表示，受委托企业遭攻击后，超过1.3万条咨询资料可能外泄。日本10月1日起已实施“主动网络防御”制度，在特定情况下允许警方或自卫队对攻击源服务器采取技术措施。政府正考虑进一步强化网络安全的集中指挥和主动处置能力。

关键词: 
日本

item.title: “23:59:60”这一特殊时间戳，今后将不再出现，2027年5月20日起，全球范围内停止插入闰秒
item.description:
@央视财经
“23:59:60”这一特殊时间戳，今后将不再出现。记者近日从国家市场监督管理总局获悉，10月13日至15日在法国凡尔赛召开的第28届国际计量大会（CGPM）通过决议，自2027年5月20日起全球范围内停止插入闰秒，将协调世界时（UTC）与基于地球自转的世界时（UT1）的最大允许偏差放宽至3600秒（1小时）。这意味着，运行了半个多世纪的闰秒机制正式退出历史舞台。
对中国而言，取消闰秒将直接降低多个关键领域的运行风险。中国时间频率机构的守时授时系统不再需要插入闰秒；5G基站、电网相量同步、金融时间戳等不再处理插入正负闰秒，运行的连续性和可靠性提升；北斗卫星导航系统设计方案中不再需要插入闰秒，会减少时间坐标转换出错的可能性。

本期编辑 徐滁


平台地址：http://www.jintiankansha.me/t/KveeKpK3p5

item.title: 以色列大选前夕爆发大规模示威，民调显示内塔尼亚胡与对手势均力敌
item.description:
澎湃新闻记者 南博一

当地时间2026年10月23日，以色列特拉维夫，一名行人经过一块竞选广告牌。广告牌左侧是以色列总理内塔尼亚胡，右侧是其主要竞争对手、反对派候选人加迪·艾森科特，广告牌上的希伯来文写着“竞争激烈”。视觉中国 图

当地时间24日，数千人聚集在以色列特拉维夫参加大规模反政府示威活动。此次抗议正值以色列议会选举前夕，而即将举行的选举被广泛视为对总理内塔尼亚胡的一次全民公投。

据央视新闻报道，以色列将于10月27日举行议会选举。这是2023年10月7日新一轮巴以冲突爆发以来，以色列首次举行全国大选。执政近20年的总理内塔尼亚胡正面临严峻挑战，最新民调显示选情充满悬念。

此次抗议活动由“十月委员会”发起，该组织由巴以冲突中以色列遇难者家属和被扣押人质家属共同创建，旨在追究当局未能阻止巴勒斯坦伊斯兰抵抗运动（哈马斯）袭击的责任。据《国土报》报道，以色列其他地区也有抗议者聚集。

“十月委员会”在集会前于社交平台X上写道：“在大选前三天，我们将举行这场标志性活动，纪念三年来为揭露真相、追究责任和推动建立国家调查委员会所进行的不懈抗争。”该组织同时提醒执法部门警惕亲政府煽动者可能制造的挑衅行为。

68岁的市民哈达斯·福伊尔什坦在集会开始前对媒体表示：“过去四年领导我们的人干得太糟糕了。以色列从未陷入过如此的困境。”

多名反对党领导人也参与了此次活动，其中包括民主党领袖亚伊尔·戈兰和中右翼政治人物加迪·艾森科特，后者是内塔尼亚胡在本次大选中的主要竞争对手。据《以色列时报》报道，当艾森科特抵达特拉维夫集会现场时，人群高呼：“谁来了？下一任总理！”

艾森科特曾担任以色列国防军总参谋长，在本次大选主打政治诚信、政府问责，主张限制总理任期，试图与内塔尼亚胡长期主导的政治风格形成鲜明对比。

此次集会的背景是，以色列民间社会和反对党多年来持续呼吁成立独立调查委员会，彻查导致2023年10月7日事件发生的安全失误。历史上，以色列在调查重大国家层面的失败时，通常都会成立类似的独立机构。

然而，内塔尼亚胡与极右翼盟友组成的联合政府拒绝了这一要求，转而提议成立一个“政治性”委员会。该委员会一半成员由政府任命，另一半成员由反对派议员任命。反对派领导人明确表示，将抵制这一由政客主导的委员会。

民意调查显示，以色列大选选情异常胶着。自2022年底以来一直执政的内塔尼亚胡右翼阵营与艾森科特阵营势均力敌。在23日晚间民调禁令生效前公布的最新数据显示，两大阵营均无法在以色列议会中单独获得多数席位。

内塔尼亚胡1996年首次出任以色列总理，此后累计执政近19年。《卫报》指出，如今以色列政治的主要分野，已不再是传统的左右翼之争，而是支持内塔尼亚胡与反对内塔尼亚胡两大阵营之间的对抗。

日本共同社23日报道称，以色列选前最后一次民调显示，反内塔尼亚胡阵营略占上风。以色列《晚祷报》23日公布的最终民调结果显示，内塔尼亚胡阵营预计将获得议会120个席位中的48席，而反内塔尼亚胡阵营则有望获得54席。一周前的民调中，双方预计都将获得51席。多家电视台23日报道的民调结果也印证了这一趋势，显示反内塔尼亚胡阵营目前处于领先地位。组阁门槛为61席。


本期编辑 徐滁


平台地址：http://www.jintiankansha.me/t/aSp5RjLJjl

item.title: 利雅德机场局部恢复运行 胡塞继续发动导弹无人机袭击
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

沙特阿拉伯首都利雅德哈立德国王国际机场10月25日部分恢复运行，此前机场因胡塞武装连续袭击关闭约两周。机场方面表示，1号航站楼恢复国内航班，2号航站楼用于本国航空公司国际航班，并要求旅客出发前确认航班状态。10月10日胡塞袭击曾造成13人死亡、300多人受伤。

不过，机场恢复当天，利雅德再次响起防空警报和爆炸声。沙特领导的联军称，防空部队拦截了一枚飞向利雅德的弹道导弹和无人机，并在南部地区击落10枚弹道导弹及一枚飞向海米斯穆谢特的巡航导弹。

胡塞军事发言人叶海亚·萨里则再次宣布哈立德国王国际机场仍是其“军事目标”，警告航空公司和旅客不要使用该机场。沙特与胡塞近期冲突持续升级，机场、能源设施及其他重要目标接连遭袭，地区航空和市场运行受到明显冲击。

关键词: 
沙特

item.title: 全球最大“电力超市”，正式开业
item.description:
10月24日，南方区域电力市场正式运行，这是目前世界上最大、最繁忙的“电力超市”。广东、广西、云南、贵州、海南五省区市场经营主体注册数量已经超过29万家，约占全国总量四分之一，将在同一个市场上开展常态化交易。


从试点探索到正式运行，南方区域电力市场迈出“关键一步”，全国统一电力市场体系建设也迎来新进展。到2030年，全国统一电力市场体系将基本建成。


一个覆盖多个省区的电力市场，到底怎么运行？答案正从三方面显现。


五省区“一盘棋”

电力跨省流动更顺畅


过去，不同省份之间存在市场规则差异和省间壁垒。自2025年6月启动连续结算试运行至今，在南方区域电力市场，发电企业、售电公司、电力用户等各类经营主体同台竞争，包括煤电、水电、核电、风电、光伏、气电等在内的全电源类型，开始在同一套规则下竞价，统一形成价格。



南方区域电力市场规模在持续扩大。


今年1至9月，南方区域电力市场累计交易电量近9000亿千瓦时，占全网售电量比例超七成；新增售电量中，有四成由新能源提供；最大单日出清电量超40亿千瓦时。


规则统一后，电力跨省、跨时空流动更加顺畅，资源也能在更大范围内实现优化配置。


居民电价不受影响

企业用电可“选套餐”


市场打通之后，居民和农业用户电价不会受到影响。


而对工商业用户来说，则可以选择更适合自身需求的用电套餐。


关注用电成本稳定性和绿电可溯源性的外向型企业和加工增值企业，参与市场、签订绿电合约的意愿明显增强。


一批数据中心、冷链物流、免税消费、国际会展等重点客户，也开始主动对接分时价格信号，优化生产班次。



与此同时，售电公司的经营模式也在变化。随着批发和零售价差空间趋于合理、零售市场风险管控持续加强，售电公司的经营逻辑正从单纯的价差套利，转向能效诊断、绿电采购、碳资产管理等增值服务。


电力市场竞争的重点，正在从单纯“卖电”，转向“怎么用好电”。



每15分钟更新价格

考验发电企业“硬功夫”


发电端的变化更加直接。在南方区域电力市场，价格信号每15分钟真实反映一次供需情况。过去，发电机组更多关注“发多少电”；现在，则要进一步计算“什么时候发、怎么发更划算”。


尤其是新能源企业，新能源上网电量全面进入市场后，项目的收益水平越来越取决于中长期合约锁价能力和现货报价能力这两项“硬功夫”。


有电力企业表示，要告别“政策推着走”的模式，转向在市场里主动搏击。



专家表示，预计南方区域今冬明春电力供需总体平衡。南方区域电力市场将进一步推动电力资源优化配置，为电力保供提供有力支撑。


从省际电力流动，到企业购电、电厂发电，一套更加统一的市场规则，正在覆盖电力生产和消费的更多环节。


南方区域电力市场转入正式运行，意味着全国统一电力市场体系建设继续提速：让电力在更大范围内流动，让价格更真实地反映供需，也让市场在资源配置中发挥更大作用。

item.title: 华盛顿“关门”，困住的是自己的未来
item.description:
当许多国家的资本加速流向中国时，被本国规则束缚的美国投资者，只能眼看机会窗口收窄。华盛顿需要认真听一听美国农民、药企和投资者的心声，算一算限制的代价


美国财政部近日发布新版对外投资限制拟议规则，公开征求意见至12月7日。规则在原有的半导体、人工智能、量子计算等设限领域外，拟将超级计算、高超音速系统等纳入管制并细化，同时新增了生物技术，并将中国等国列为“受关注国家”。10月24日，中国商务部回应指出，美方歧视性扩大对华投资限制范围，加大限制力度，是典型的泛化国家安全做法，违背两国元首达成的重要共识，中方对此表示严重关切、坚决反对，并保留采取相应措施的权利。


美国对华投资管制步步收紧，实质是借泛化安全概念遏制中国新兴产业。从2023年的行政命令，到2025年国会立法扩大适用范围，再到此次新增生物技术领域，其逻辑一脉相承——试图以切断资本流动延缓中国科技进步。讽刺的是，新纳入管制的生物技术恰恰是中美互利合作最活跃的领域之一。全球在研新药约1/3源自中国，辉瑞、百时美施贵宝等美国药企今年已与中国合作伙伴达成数十亿美元的许可协议，而美国制药行业因反对华盛顿推出严格的投资限制，已进行了为期数月的游说。以安全之名行保护主义之实，首先捆住的正是美国投资者自己的手脚。


数据显示，华盛顿的政策取向与多数美国企业的市场选择正背道而驰。中国商务部数据显示，1—9月，来自美国、韩国、法国、瑞士等来源地的投资继续增长，其中美国增长7.7%。尽管政治噪音不断，多数美国企业仍以真金白银为中国市场投下信任票。但另一方面，7.7%的增速明显低于法国的31.8%、瑞士的26%，不难看到华盛顿限制措施对企业决策的负面影响。美中贸易全国委员会2026年度报告显示，95%的受访美企认为在华业务对维持其全球竞争力有从“一定”到“非常重要”的意义。市场自发投票的方向，与政策设计者用力拉拽的方向，恰好相反。


关上大门的国家，失去的往往是自己的机会，这一规律正被事实反复印证。美中贸易全国委员会调查显示，去年美国对华出口下降26%，约14.8万个就业岗位随之消失；受本国出口管制影响的美企中，61%眼看市场份额流向竞争对手。国际数据公司（IDC）预测，到2030年，华盛顿的贸易限制可能使美国人形机器人市场规模比原本应有规模缩小近60%。“一旦市场失守，就很难再夺回”，这是美国工商界自己的提醒。与之相对，中国1—9月高技术产业引资增长33.8%，外资利润再投资同比增长4.7%，超大规模市场的磁力有增无减。当世界许多国家的资本加速流向中国时，被本国规则束缚的美国投资者，只能眼看机会窗口收窄。


中美经贸关系的本质是互利共赢，不能让政治化、泛安全化的逆流冲击两国关系大局。中美两国元首的战略引领、工商界苦心经营的合作纽带，不应被一纸拟议规则所侵蚀。中美合作关乎两国人民福祉，也关乎全球产业链供应链稳定与世界经济增长。给正常商业活动贴上“威胁”标签、把资本流动当武器，动摇的不只是企业信心，更是国际经贸秩序的根基。


规则尚在征求意见阶段，最终文本未定，美国工商界的理性声音理应被听见。中方在保留随时采取反制措施权利的同时，将继续以高水平对外开放对冲外部不确定性，“投资中国就是投资未来”的成色只会更足。华盛顿需要认真听一听美国农民、药企和投资者的心声，算一算限制的代价。用来绊住别人脚步的绳索，往往先缠住自己的双手。中美合则两利、斗则俱伤，这个朴素的道理，值得华盛顿重新掂量。



本文系环球时报社评

item.title: ICE said a man jumped on the hood of their vehicle. Video — and police — say otherwise.
item.description:
When footage of a man being hit by federal immigration officers’ SUV in Northern California became public, the Department of Homeland Security responded by saying the man had jumped on the vehicle’s hood.

Local police raised doubts about federal officials’ account as they announced a criminal investigation into Tuesday morning’s incident involving the pedestrian, 37-year-old Antonio Moreida, citing video footage that contradicted DHS’ statement.

Footage from a nearby surveillance camera, a bystander’s cellphone recording and Moreida’s GoPro, which had already been made public at the time of the agency’s statement, told a different story of what happened on a residential street in Woodland, an agricultural city just outside of Sacramento. The incident is the latest in which DHS’ account has been contradicted by officials and video evidence amid the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.

Police contradict ICE account

In a statement Wednesday morning, DHS said Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers didn’t hit a pedestrian.

“An agitator jumped onto the hood of an ICE vehicle and the officer driving applied the brakes,” a DHS spokesperson said in a statement in response to CNN’s request for information. “The agitator slid off the hood. ICE immediately contacted EMS and the Woodland Police Department. Flopping for the camera is dangerous, especially when it interferes with a federal law enforcement operation,” apparently accusing the man of faking his injuries.

After the incident on Tuesday, Woodland Police Chief Ryan Kinnan said in a statement he found footage of the incident troubling. Investigators were working to gather evidence and statements and to review available audio and video related to the incident, including video taken from multiple perspectives, police said in a Facebook post. Woodland Police didn’t take part in the ICE operation the agents were involved in that morning, police said.

The following day, Woodland Police called DHS’ account “inconsistent.”

“Certain claims made in the DHS statement are inconsistent with the video evidence obtained and reviewed by Woodland Police investigators,” Kinnan said in an update Wednesday. The update said investigators had established, based on video evidence, the pedestrian had been hit by the vehicle driven by ICE agents and that he had not jumped onto the vehicle.

The local police department is conducting a criminal investigation into the events leading up to the collision and the actions of those involved, Kinnan said Wednesday.

By Thursday, in response to follow-up questions about the video footage, federal officials no longer said the person jumped on the hood.

“This individual chose to directly impede a law enforcement action and stand in the middle of an active road,” an ICE spokesperson said in a statement to CNN. “Our officers deliberately attempted to avoid making contact with this anti-ice protestor and drive around him, while also braking. We strongly urge individuals to not stand in the middle of active roadways while a law enforcement vehicle is approaching.”

What footage shows

Footage reviewed by CNN shows Moreida, a Woodland resident, in the middle of the street at around 9:40 a.m. Tuesday. Moreida said he had responded to a call that morning by NorCal Resist, a group which monitors immigration operations, about ICE activity in Woodland, he told CNN on Tuesday, hours after the incident.

unknown content item

-

He said he was trying to record agents’ unmarked vehicles. He had been recording one vehicle, standing on the car’s driver’s side, when it turned left and drove off, which he said pushed him into the middle of the street.

Video from Moreida’s GoPro shows him following a black Dodge Durango with tinted windows as it drives down the street.

Then, he said he heard a loud engine before seeing the agents’ black Chevy Tahoe drive toward him, which is shown in his GoPro footage, though the video has no audio.

unknown content item

-

Down the street, the bystander’s cellphone video shows the Durango pass the Tahoe, which has tinted windows, on a residential street. In the video’s background, people can be heard blowing whistles, presumably to alert people nearby of ICE’s presence in the neighborhood.

The ICE agent driving the Tahoe moves toward Moreida and between the cars with its brake lights on, footage shows. In the bystander’s video, Moreida isn’t yet visible.

The SUV’s wheels begin to turn to the left only a few feet from Moreida, a wider angle of surveillance footage from a home shows.

unknown content item

-

“The individual was standing in the street long enough that a reasonable person should be able to see them and recognize that they were there,” said Ryan Schwank, a former ICE attorney and training instructor who reviewed the videos provided by CNN.

Schwank also took issue with ICE’s characterization that Moreida was standing in the middle of an active road and impeding law enforcement’s actions.

“When we’re looking at Antonio’s actions, he’s not impeding. He’s not standing blocking the vehicle from moving,” he said. “He’s standing and filming, and that’s well within his bounds to do. He’s well within his rights to do what he was doing.”

Moreida’s GoPro appears to show when he’s struck by the front-right side of the vehicle before he drops his camera.

“Before I knew it, it just drove straight into me,” he said. “I took the hood of the car straight to the chest. It initially took the wind out of me and I couldn’t breathe.”

The surveillance footage shows Moreida take a step back when he appears to make contact with the car. He is then seen falling toward the ground, off the front-right side of the car, the footage shows.

In the bystander’s footage from behind, a screeching noise is heard before the Tahoe jolts forward. The SUV veers left before straightening out, the video shows.

The bystander’s angle shows the Tahoe brake lights turn off. Moreida is then visible in the bystander’s video, falling to the ground and rolling, first on his back with his legs swinging above him. He then appears seated upright in the nearby surveillance footage, this time facing the sidewalk.

The SUV’s brake lights turn back on briefly before it drives farther down the street, the surveillance footage shows.

The driver, an ICE agent, stayed near the scene and called local dispatch, Woodland Police said. The agent cooperated with police during the initial investigation, the local agency said.

Moreida said an off-duty EMT provided him aid at the scene before Woodland Police officers arrived. Federal agents didn’t approach him after he was hit by the SUV, he said.

Moreida said he was eventually transported to the hospital. He said he had X-rays taken of his swollen knees, where he said he had the most damage. In addition, he said he has bruises and cuts from the road.

ICE has reduced the amount of training for officers, including in vehicle operations and how to deal with confrontations, said Schwank, who is now an agency whistleblower after resigning in February.

On Saturday, ICE said it is instituting additional training for officers.

“ICE training will now be extending to 72 days. The change, effective June 2, 2026, will apply to all new academy classes beginning July 1, 2026. All graduates of the previous academy curriculum will attend follow-on training at the Advanced Field Officer Training Program,” an ICE spokesperson said in an emailed statement to CNN. “As we have said all along, ICE training does not end when recruits graduate from the academy. ICE officers go through a rigorous on-the-job training and mentorship. This additional training is tracked online and monitored closely.”

Local officials call for investigations

Soon after it became public, local officials expressed dismay over the incident, which occurred in a rural Northern California community that’s about half Latino. More than a fifth of the population is foreign-born, according to US Census estimates.

“The lack of truth in the Department of Homeland Security’s statement is evidenced by video taken at the scene,” Woodland Mayor Tom Stallard said in a statement issued Wednesday. “All of us can be assured that the Police Department’s investigation into this disturbing incident will continue to be speedy, fair, and impartial.”

US Rep. Mike Thompson, a Democrat whose district includes Woodland, said ICE’s statements about the facts surrounding the incident were disappointing but not surprising.

“ICE has a history of trying to hide the facts and mislead the public,” he told CNN. “And this is another example of that happening.”

On the day of the operation, Thompson called on Acting ICE Director David Venturella to investigate the collision, including by preserving evidence and cooperating with local authorities. As of Friday, the congressman had yet to receive a response to his letter, his office told CNN.

CNN’s Taylor Galgano contributed to this report.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/25/us/woodland-man-struck-by-ice-vehicle

item.title: 失语的皇后：“每一位权臣都借她之口诉说野心”
item.description:
2026-10-25 23:00:00

《南齐书·皇后传》书影，中华再造善本丛书影印宋刻元明初递修本 图/受访者提供

如果只看史书的记录，王宝明，这位南齐的文安皇后是中国历史上最专权的女性之一。

丈夫新丧不久，她便废黜了两位皇帝，而后推立了日后的齐明帝萧鸾。在南齐灭亡前，又是王宝明将昏君萧宝卷黜落为东昏侯，并以太后的身份临朝称制，将南齐帝位禅让于梁武帝萧衍。

历史的真相是，她不过是双簧演员，每一位权臣都借太后之口诉说野心。斧钺在侧，她除了配合别无选择：在王宝明口中“宜入承宝命”的萧鸾，杀害了她的亲生骨肉郁林王萧昭业；操纵王宝明禅让时，萧衍已将南齐皇帝东昏侯的首级置于案前。

真正的王宝明在历史中失语了。《南齐书·皇后传》用短促的两千余字概述了九位皇后的生平，是书中最简练的传记之一。至于王宝明的一生，史官仅着墨二百余字。她是王妃、皇太子妃、皇后、太后，但除了政治身份，史书对她的唯一描述只有她的失宠。

“四年，为皇太子妃，无宠。太子为宫人制新丽衣裳及首饰，而后床帷陈设故旧，钗镊十余枚。”

在四川大学历史系副教授郭硕看来，史书中的王宝明只是浮现在政治漩涡中心的影子，人们以她的名字讲话，“但我们听不到她的声音。”

十多年前，还是博士生的郭硕与老师、同门修订中华书局版《南齐书》点校本时，发现史料中以王宝明名义留下的文书繁多，体量冠绝南北朝女性，但它们皆假手于文人，王宝明的所思所想未有片语在册。郭硕想要记录“失语”的来龙去脉，但因材料匮乏、思考未周，迟迟未能下笔。

郭硕（后排左二）与《南齐书》修订组同仁的合照 图/受访者提供

直到近年与编辑讨论时，他们一致认为将弱者置于写作中心应是学界努力的方向，郭硕因而重拾了王宝明的故事。

2026年秋，郭硕的新书《失语的皇后：南齐权力嬗变中的个体生命》出版，他希望透过王宝明的故事，“让某些在历史尘埃中湮没无声的弱者，获得在宏大的历史背景下被理解、被共情的机会。”

“未亡人不幸，骤此百罹”

王宝明出身于南朝顶级士族琅琊王氏，而她身处的恰是一个极重门第的时代。

永嘉年间，中原战乱，西晋皇室仓皇南渡。王导为延续司马氏政权立下不世之功，琅琊王氏因之骤贵，时人谓“王与马，共天下”。

承先人遗荫，王宝明的父、祖在晋宋之际各有官秩。与王宝明相比，丈夫萧长懋的兰陵萧氏略逊一筹，在门第观念森严的南朝，这样的婚姻绝属罕见。巧合的是，王宝明的父亲与萧长懋的祖父萧道成——南齐开国皇帝，曾同在太宰府中为官，正是这场共事之谊促成了一桩失类的婚姻。

随着宋明帝离世，各方力量蠢蠢欲动。在平叛中，萧道成的势力日益壮大，王宝明则随着夫家在乱世中几经辗转。终于在公元479年，萧道成受禅建立南齐，王宝明因皇帝嫡长孙正妻的身份获封为南郡王妃。

14年后，她在政治上的无限荣宠戛然而止，丈夫萧长懋未及继位便病逝。同年，王宝明的儿子萧昭业继位，她从太子妃变成了太后。不久，顾命大臣萧鸾便率兵入宫，当众弑君，而后立萧长懋次子萧昭文为帝，再逼其让位于己，礼成后亦杀之。

儿子死后，王宝明第一次“干涉”朝政。在太后令中，她严厉批评了萧昭业失德日久，又称赞萧鸾所为是家国之福。

萧鸾继位后，王宝明迁入鄱阳王故居，改名为宣德宫。在世时，人们又称她为宣德皇后，或宣德太后。每当权臣欲行废立之事，史笔便称其为“太后”；当新帝登基，诏书中又抑之为“皇后”，这意味着王宝明失去了作为太后左右前朝的法理基础。

日藏弘文本《文馆词林》所见南齐明帝即位诏书，有“宣德皇后”字样 图/受访者提供

定宫名为“宣德”，恐怕是王宝明一生为数不多的能做主之事，这正是她为南郡王妃时居所之名。但悠闲的日子回不去了。在半监禁的岁月里，萧鸾将王宝明的属官刘朗之免职禁锢，又迁毁了太庙中其夫文惠太子的神位。

后来，萧鸾的儿子东昏侯为下人所害，梁武帝萧衍又将王宝明推上前台，作为齐梁禅让的遮羞布。在最后一道废黜皇帝的太后令中，代笔之人以王宝明的口吻写道：“未亡人不幸，骤此百罹，感念存没，心焉如割。奈何！奈何！”

梁武帝萧衍的半身像轴，中国台北故宫博物院藏 图/资料图片

遗憾的是，这声嗟叹来自于作为政治符号的宣德太后，而王宝明作为“人”的悲喜，永远湮没在了历史的后台。

不论是作为读者，抑或是历史研究者，郭硕都喜欢有感情的史学。他喜欢《史记》的《屈原贾生列传》《淮阴侯列传》，理由是司马迁写出了“人味”：作为人的无奈和不得已。

在《失语的皇后》中，他以弱者为中心的写法，源自历史学家唐长孺《〈晋书·赵至传〉中所见的曹魏士家制度》一文的启发。文章讲述了出身于兵士之家的赵至，被户籍制度逼得呕血而亡的悲剧。

郭硕试图以小见大，重构王宝明被权力结构裹挟的一生：“太后的身份起了什么作用，她如何被权臣利用，怎样的规训让她没有抵抗，她的声音又如何被结构消磨掉？”

以下内容源自我们与郭硕的对话和他的新书，关于王宝明和那个动荡的时代，以及史书中无数的失语者。

郭硕 图/受访者提供

被操纵的政治符号

南方人物周刊：如何理解“失语”的含义？

郭硕：失语就是别人替她说话，她自己不能说话。史书中提到王宝明的次数特别多，以她的名义发布的诏令也很多，看起来像专权的皇太后一样，每次废立都要参与，但实际上只是来签字画押的。女性，或者说皇后的失语是机制性问题，同时期北魏的文明太后也在失语，但情况与王宝明正好相反。文明太后可以左右孝文帝的朝政，是能够掌控一切的女性，但在史书中她被强行消音，她的主张被皇帝、群臣代言了，没有直接用她的口吻说出，她的传记也只有一千多字。

南方人物周刊：王宝明谥号“文安”，“文”源自丈夫的谥号，如何理解萧梁专门给她的谥号“安”？

郭硕：《逸周书·谥法解》说，“好和不争曰安。” “安”是萧梁对她的肯定，如果没有王宝明，梁武帝的局面会困难很多。萧衍以雍州刺史的身份起兵，到首都建康（今江苏南京）后围而不攻，想等东昏侯出城投降，结果东昏侯被手下的人杀了。此时还有一个被萧颖胄拥立的齐和帝远在荆州，萧衍缺少政治上的合法性，因而在犹豫禅让的事。这时候沈约告诉他，“岂复有人方更同公作贼？”意思是再拖下去萧衍就要变成反贼了，还借用曹操的话说“不可慕虚名而处实祸”。因此萧衍让王宝明废掉东昏侯，并将齐和帝控制在姑孰（今安徽当涂），让王宝明以太后临朝称制的方式，完成了“皇帝缺席的禅让”。

南方人物周刊：王宝明代替皇帝行使权力、实行禅让的政治合法性是什么？

郭硕：此前有太后废立皇帝的先例，但没有太后禅让的先例，这是齐梁禅代的特殊之处。王宝明的政治合法性来自皇帝的权威。她是前朝皇帝的配偶、当朝皇帝的嫡母。家国一体是传统政治文化的核心，那么就会有母权——注意不是女权。王宝明只有先成为先皇遗孀，才能代表前朝皇帝行使权力。通常，母权在皇帝无法亲政时才会出现，比如吕后或者慈禧太后，皇帝一旦掌控权力，太后的权力就不存在了。尽管制度层面是限制女性的，但个别能力强、有权威的女性，就算儿子成年了她也控制得住。武则天就是这样，她甚至亲自当皇帝。慈禧不愿意还权，还与光绪发生了斗争，北魏冯太后跟孝文帝也有分歧。

南方人物周刊：萧衍已经掌握了都城和百官，为什么仍然要通过禅让获得权力？

郭硕：禅让最初形成于儒家的政治理想，就是所谓“舜禹之事”，这个制度在中国历史上延续了近八百年，最早王莽就做过，从曹丕禅汉开始，一直到宋代建立才结束。通过禅让过渡权力变成了一种政治惯性，后面宋、元因为战争灭亡都是特殊情况。汉代以后禅让不仅是政治问题，也是信仰世界的问题。每个朝代代表了五行中不同的德，如果是以“汤武革命”的方式易代，两个朝代的五行就是相克的，而禅让的话五行就是相生的。禅让变成了一个我从哪里来的问题，人们会觉得如果王朝不是按照五行生克产生的，就不符合天道运行的规律了。

南方人物周刊：萧鸾继位时也借助了王宝明的权威，但他的情况跟萧衍还不太一样。

郭硕：这些权臣活干得太糙了。魏晋易代的时候，司马家让贾充手下的成济杀了皇帝，宋齐易代，萧道成也是买通皇帝的侍卫暗杀，而萧鸾带领禁军大摇大摆进入皇宫把皇帝杀了，这是没有先例的，在道德方面就是篡逆。大家都看到了，不可能把在场的所有目击者都清洗掉。他必须要有一块遮羞布，不然没法服人心。怎么办？这时候皇帝的母亲发布令书，说我儿子是道德败坏的昏君，感谢萧鸾把他杀了，这对萧鸾来说太重要了。后来北魏孝文帝问南朝使臣，萧鸾废郁林王的依据，使臣说“上逼太后之严令”，将责任推卸到王宝明身上，言外之意是郁林王得罪了太后才被杀。萧鸾颠倒黑白，通过太后令将暴力篡弑变成了合法继承，对于被控制的王宝明来说，估计是非常痛苦的。

南方人物周刊：面对权臣的胁迫，同时代与王宝明身份相近的女性是怎么做的？

郭硕：东晋的穆章何皇后经历了桓玄篡位，刘宋的恭皇后王贞风经历了宋齐禅代，她们与王宝明面临着类似的环境但行为不一样。王宝明是配合的，何皇后是到太庙前大哭，“哀感路人”，气得桓玄说，“天下禅代常理，何预何氏女子事耶！”王贞风则是想尽办法杀掉萧道成，袁粲、沈攸之、刘晃、刘绰、卜伯兴反对萧道成的背后都有她的影子。她们都是反抗者，命运也很悲惨，后来何皇后被刘裕控制起来，不让她“奉拜陵庙”，萧道成即位后，王贞风在短时间内就原因不明地死掉了，不像王宝明在齐梁禅代后还活了十多年。

齐高祖萧道成半身像，中国台北故宫博物院藏 图/资料图片

南方人物周刊：为什么王宝明的选择与她们截然相反？

郭硕：王宝明与她们是有关联的，也有一种宿命感。在很长的时间里，她居住的东宫就是何皇后曾经的永安宫，所以她一定听说过何皇后的故事。在宋齐禅代之际，昔日的太后王贞风死了，王宝明成为了南郡王妃，她们都来自琅琊王氏，她也能看到、听到王贞风的经历。她们的悲惨结局会不会影响王宝明的选择？是拼一把就死，还是活下来，这个读者们可以想象一下。当然王宝明的选择也跟她顺从的性格有关。到后来齐梁禅代的时候，她可能已经心如死灰了。萧衍曾经暗示南齐宗室，杀掉萧鸾一脉也算给高帝、武帝子孙复仇了，这个话对于王宝明来说也是这样的，所以她不太会反抗。

南方人物周刊：为什么历史上权力更迭的时代会有更多人关注，它的吸引力来自哪里？

郭硕：这种生死危急之际的选择，最能够凸显人性。比如著名诗人谢脁向齐明帝告发自己的岳父王敬则谋反，后来老婆每天带着刀要找谢脁报杀父之仇，谢脁有家不敢回。最终他也因遭人诬陷被杀，死前他后悔揭发岳父，感叹“我不杀王公，王公由我而死”。

“权力结构中的每一重身份都淹没了她”

南方人物周刊：你似乎对王宝明有莫大的同情，比如“我宁愿相信，这是王宝明母子的政敌，有意将宋孝武帝乱伦和山阴公主养面首之事，稍加改动加在王宝明身上”，对历史学这一强调客观、严谨的学科而言，学者对研究对象动容是一件好事吗？

郭硕：个人的感情不可能不影响历史写作。分析历史哲学之父布莱德雷就强调：“历史学家不可能只是被动的接受者，或仅仅是复现者。”忠实地转述信息是不可能的。爱德华·卡尔在《历史是什么》中讲述了魏玛共和国外交官施特雷泽曼的故事：施特雷泽曼大部分的时间都用于处理与苏联的关系，但是秘书整理档案时，将多数涉苏内容删除，留下的大部分是欧美档案。整理者是有偏向的。历史学家有选择、有判断，就一定会带有立场，选择记忆或遗忘什么的时候，批判就已经开始了。

道德、感情也是历史学问题意识的来源。如果没有对女性苦难的感触，或者意识到女性被遗忘了，就无法出现女性史的研究。所以柯林武德讲，“一切历史都是思想史……历史学家必须在自己的心灵中重演过去的思想。”有了这种想象的共情，接近过去的行动者及其处境，才能理解人物的行为。如果用冷漠的态度对待笔下的人，就是把古人的悲喜当成了死的材料、冷冰冰的数据。感情和伦理首先是用来抵抗遗忘的，其次是防止历史人物遭受二次伤害。王宝明本来就是被伤害、被欺辱的无声的人，不能再用史笔伤害她，一次又一次把政治对手给她炮制的宫闱丑闻，毫无反思地加诸其身。

南方人物周刊：近些年许多历史写作都聚焦于传统权力结构中被忽视的人物，这种转移是怎样发生的？

郭硕：从帝王将相转向边缘人物，本质上是从研究民族国家的经济、政治，转向了多元社会。最早的时候历史学者认为既然自然科学有规律，就可以追寻社会发展的宏大规律。19世纪以来的兰克史学（强调客观地重建过去）就是与民族、国家这些宏大问题绑定的。20世纪以后历史写作从帝王将相、战争、外交转向边缘人物，我觉得最重要的因素是马克思主义。它涉及工人运动，因此会关注劳工大众的生活，比如汤普森的《英国工人阶级的形成》。西方也出现了殖民地的独立浪潮、民权运动、女权运动、学生运动、身份政治等等，这些也会影响到史学写作。后来的年鉴学派、新文化史也关注边缘人物，比如勒华拉杜里的《蒙塔尤》、金茨堡的《奶酪与蛆虫》、娜塔莉·泽蒙·戴维斯的《马丁·盖尔归来》。最近比较火的还有刘永华《程允亨的19世纪》。

南方人物周刊：在新的写作潮流中，围绕帝王将相的史学会消失吗，或者会有什么新变？

郭硕：帝王将相不会消失，政治史中也会有新政治史、帝国史、全球史，《康熙的红票》就是全球史的代表作。改变的是我们问的问题，不再按照“成王败寇”的逻辑问谁是统治者、谁夺取了天下，而是权力结构是什么，权力如何以一种制度性的方式运作，弱者在结构中是什么位置、怎么生活。

南方人物周刊：“成王败寇”的观念会对认识历史有什么影响？

郭硕：成王败寇历史观的问题是把胜利变成了正当性。我赢了，我就有天意。研究者会偏向成功者叙事，带有明显的“慕强”倾向，这种叙事会消解个人真实的生命历程。比如齐明帝萧鸾和梁武帝萧衍都得位不正，但萧鸾的形象比萧衍差多了。梁武帝后来稳固统治了几十年，这个国家似乎治理得还算可以，所以梁武帝的形象就好很多，他是成功者。而从南齐的覆灭来看，萧鸾就是典型的失败者。北魏的文明太后也是这样，在古代她是被批判、被污名化的女性，但为什么今天她的地位那么高，因为她参与了孝文帝的汉化改革，这被认为是民族融合中非常重要的一环。当然今天的历史研究也不是为了翻案，不会因为这个人失败了就把他说得很好。

《南齐书·皇后传》书影，清乾隆四年武英殿刊本，郭硕藏书 图/受访者提供

南方人物周刊：你在书中只能呈现出王宝明失语的状态，但没有办法让她发出声音。

郭硕：我只能在权力结构中将她浮现出来，但浮现的是一个影子，我们听不到她的声音了。南朝女性的史料极少，中古时期连地方志都很少，也不像北朝有不少墓志，比如洛阳的邙山一带出土了大量的墓志，南朝连墓区都发现得很少，即便有墓志，不过是男性作者的代言而已，女性的声音无法留存。

南方人物周刊：写这本书的时候，期待能向读者传达什么？

郭硕：根本目的还是希望能共情被传统史学遗忘的弱者。王宝明虽然是弱者，但毕竟属于统治者，不是那个时代最悲惨的人。梁武帝占领建康后，立刻把几千宫女分给将士们，又将东昏侯的余妃送给王茂，人变成了被赠送的道具。这些人无声音、无面貌、无后续，她们是什么样的人？史料不足，我们更难想象，但至少可以注意到，历史上有余氏和宫女这样的一些人被当作工具赠送了。

南方人物周刊：在有限的史料中，怎样辨别哪些材料更可信或更有价值？

郭硕：只能在足够克制的前提下，做一点推断、猜测。尤其是宫廷内的事情，外人是完全不知道的，我会信任《南齐书》的一些内容，是因为作者萧子显在南齐王府里长大，那些涉及皇室生活的内容很有可能来自他的一手材料。史书说武穆裴皇后的公婆不喜欢她，而更喜欢庾氏，我推测庾氏应当是萧子显的妈妈，因为他总是在书中提到一些细节性的东西。有一次郁林王对庾氏说，阿婆，佛法说有福德才能出生在帝王家，现在我做了王却像有罪一般，还不如做富人。这应该就是庾氏对萧子显转述的内容。

南朝女性供养人拓片 图/受访者提供

南方人物周刊：作为男性学者写女性的生命史，会觉得有性别上的隔阂吗？

郭硕：我觉得对弱势者的共情还是可以做到的，当然性别上的隔阂也会有一些。比如我写武穆裴皇后受公婆虐待，也可能虐待作为儿媳妇的王宝明。有女同学跟我说，女性被婆婆虐待就一定会虐待儿媳妇吗？但其实史料上写过，裴皇后确实训罚过另外一个儿媳妇，我才会这样写。书中也提到一些传统史学中男性视角的偏见，比如皇后王贞风斥责宋明帝时，她的哥哥王景文就感叹：“后在家为儜弱妇人，不知今段遂能刚正如此。”后来清代史学家王鸣盛说王宝明“一妇人也，而两朝篡夺，皆托其名以欺人，真如儿戏”。话语中充满鄙夷，也有性别偏见在作怪。

南方人物周刊：为了写这本书，你有专门学习性别研究的成果吗？

郭硕：我最早是从罗伯特·达恩顿的史学著作《屠猫记》意识到性别的问题，书中写小红帽中狼外婆的原型，讨论为什么老年女性会被变成非常糟糕的形象。影响更直接的是达琳·尤施卡的《性别符号学》，特别是“女性的男性化”问题，其中有一个“猎手隐喻”：传统叙述中男性是猎人，女性是猎物。占有女性就占有了猎物，男性争夺一切权力都是为了争夺女性，女性一旦想成为成功者，就必须得模仿男性。中国历史上，花木兰就是女性的男性化。“猎物/猎手”的概念就是来自尤施卡，我写王宝明甚至都不是猎物，“只是被猎手作为擦拭血迹的抹布”。讨论“荡妇想象”问题时，我还参考了《特洛伊的海伦：女神、公主与荡妇》和约翰·盖格农的《性社会学》。

南方人物周刊：书的结尾处写道，“她的人生，无疑是一个悲剧。”你认为王宝明悲剧的根源是什么？

郭硕：权力结构中的每一重身份都淹没了她。她是高门的女儿、太子的老婆、皇帝的妈妈，这些都是别人需要的身份。因为是顶级高门，萧道成想要与王家联姻，她就成了政治婚姻的牺牲品；她是太子的老婆，就必须忍受文惠太子宠爱别的女人，把她晾在一边；她是皇帝的妈妈，儿子的政治风波就会将她卷进去，甚至儿子被杀她还要为仇家开脱。南朝史书经常说不要生活在帝王家，否则会感到很痛苦。门阀制度、皇权制度、禅让制度导致了无数的悲剧，把王宝明掏空成了一个符号。她失语了，她的声音属于别人，自己能做的就是当哑巴，沉默着过完悲剧的人生。

item.title: A strange twist in Alaska's Senate race has Trump's DOJ fighting to block results
item.description:
Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Justice Department's newly filed lawsuit to prevent Alaska state officials from certifying election results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses in November.

In an at-times contentious interview with CNN’s “State of the Union,” Blanche pointed out that according to the Constitution, Congress can create laws at any time to regulate elections. But when host Dana Bash asked what crime the administration was arguing was being committed, Blanche replied, “It depends.”

“There could be a crime,” said Blanche. “But the real wrong here is that Alaskans are going to be confused and will not have their vote heard. So an Alaskan intends to vote for one candidate, but is confused because of a second candidate with exactly the same name who has voted Democrat his entire life, who donated money to the other Democrat opponent, is running.”

Bash pressed Blanche on how it is illegal for two candidates with the same name to be on a ballot at the same time.

"It is an obligation of the states to avoid confusion, among other things, confusion in the minds of voters in the election process,” Blanche replied. “So the question is whether Alaska, by allowing this to happen, is violating the law and the federal law and the constitution by allowing confusion in the ballot."

The Alaskan Supreme Court in June ruled that both Sullivans may remain on the ballot as the incumbent faces off in a tight reelection battle with former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola. The four-person Senate ranked-choice ballot for the general election specifies that Dan S. Sullivan is a "Registered Republican" and the "incumbent" — no information is listed after Dan J. Sullivan Jr's name.

Regardless, in the suit filed Thursday, DOJ argued that Dan J. Sullivan Jr.’s name on the ballot constitutes a purposeful effort to mislead voters.

Still, it’s unclear how much the court can do about the Justice Department’s lawsuit. With ballots secret, it is virtually impossible for the Justice Department to identify specific voters and clarify which Sullivan candidate they meant to vote for.

Blanche, though, seemed unconcerned about that hurdle.

“There are a number of scenarios where it could be obvious that a voter was confused by the way they wrote down candidates,” said Blanche.

Republican groups have worked to differentiate between the two Sullivans.

President Donald Trump on Friday said the legal challenge was his idea, though Blanche on Sunday declined to state whether the president had directed him to file the suit.

"I will never talk about any communications I have with the president of the United States,” he said.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska), who is not up for reelection this year, said Friday that the lawsuit is unnecessary.

“Alaskans don’t need any help voting for their preferred candidates, and the State of Alaska has already handled this by clearly distinguishing the candidates on this year’s ballot,” Murkowski said in a post on X. “The Department of Justice should never have filed this lawsuit.”

Her comments drew the ire of Trump, who on Saturday called Murkowski “Republicans’ Worst Senator, by far,” in a post to Truth Social.

Trump said that Alaska’s ranked choice voting system is “a TOTAL DEMOCRAT SCAM meant to confuse the Voter, so that Senator Dan Sullivan will lose Votes to a man who has never participated in Politics before, named Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr.”

“He is only there because the Democrats want to steal the Election, and Murkowski probably wants that to happen, which is why she is against the DOJ filing a Lawsuit in order to stop this impending crime and tragedy,” Trump added. “I have delivered for Alaska at Historic Levels, nobody has ever seen anything like it, and all I’m asking for is a FAIR AND HONEST SENATORIAL ELECTION! Lisa Murkowski is a DISGRACE to Alaska and our Country. You just don’t get any worse!"

Democratic leaders have also widely condemned the lawsuit, arguing the president is attempting to lay the foundation to overturn the midterm election results if their candidates win critical elections — something Bash asked Blanche about on Sunday.

“One of the big questions is whether or not the president is laying the groundwork for a scenario where, whether it's Alaska or somewhere else, there is, in your words a couple of days ago, a 'doomsday scenario' and we could be in a situation where President Trump tries to overturn the election and the result of that could be, god forbid, what we saw after January 6th,” Bash said.

Blanche quickly fired back: “Oh stop it. You gotta stop it with that. You're not being a real person. You set me up. You're saying, “'Mr. Attorney General, because the president of the United States wants to stop fraud and confusion in Alaska, is he going to do something crazy?' That is not a real question.”

Bash replied that she did not think it was an unfair question, but Blanche argued that the premise of the question was untrue.

“Instead of focusing on how we can address that and how we can remedy that, you're talking about January 6th,” he said. “That's so embarrassing to this network that that's what you're talking about.”

“Oh, come on,” Bash said.

"Don't “oh, come on” me,” replied Blanche. “There's literally confusion."

It wasn’t the only tense interview Blanche had Sunday.

In an appearance on CBS’ “Face the Nation,” Blanche accused host Margaret Brennan of lying over the wording of the Justice Department’s lawsuit.

“The Alaska Supreme Court did take on this matter,” Brennan began, referring to the court’s June decision.

“No, they didn't. That's a state law,” interrupted Blanche.

“In this country, the states administer the elections. This is how the state came up with the issue and how to handle any confusion,” Brennan said as the Alaskan ballot was shown on the screen.

“You’re not telling the truth,” said Blanche.

Brennan asked why identifying Sullivan as the incumbent is insufficient for the administration.

“Well, listen, I don't know if it's sufficient,” said Blanche. “But I can tell you this: that the director of the Alaska election system has said that it will likely cause confusion.”

Brennan pointed out that the ballots are already circulating, and voting may already be underway, as many vote by mail in Alaska. She then pressed Blanche on Trump claiming responsibility for the lawsuit, to which Blanche reiterated that he will not share his communications with the president.

“The president of the United States said this on camera,” Brennan replied. “He said, "I told them to do it." Did he tell that to you?”

“He didn’t say that on camera,” argued Blanche, before adding Trump had been looking at the situation for “months and months and months.” He later added that he had “no idea” who Trump was referring to, and even if he did, he would “most certainly not” talk about it.

Brennan then pivoted to read several lines from DOJ’s lawsuit, including that the suit defined voter confusion as Sen. Sullivan not winning the election and that had all votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan been cast for the incumbent then he would have won.

As she spoke, Blanche interrupted again.

“That’s not what it says,” he said.

“I’m quoting from it,” Brennan replied, holding up a printed version of the suit. “You are telling them not to certify it. What right does the federal government have telling a state not to certify or how to certify?”

After a moment of crosstalk, Blanche stated: "If you talk the whole time you're not going to get answers out of me. If you let me answer your question I can address your question." He then said the suit does not call for officials to avoid certifying the election.

“All we're doing is trying to put guardrails in place so that if that happens there's a system allowed where the ballots are kept in a way so we can determine whether there was confusion,” he explained.

In his interview with CNN, Blanche denied any political motivations were behind the Justice Department’s lawsuit.

“It's important the American people understand that we are not — President Trump is not trying to take over a state election in any way, shape or form,” he said. “What we're trying to do is make it clear that if it is obvious after the election, that confusion led to an improper and illegal result that the Alaskan system should be able to address that.”

In an interview with NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday, Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) argued the administration has no standing to bring the Alaska lawsuit, and he lambasted Blanche for leading a “disgraceful campaign.”

“This suit has no chance of succeeding,” said Schiff. “But the fact that Todd Blanche and the Justice Department are willing to go along with it, they're willing to put their name on it, is an indication of how far they will go after this election is over to try to challenge the results.”

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/25/blanche-alaska-lawsuit-could-be-crime-01134861

item.title: How the conservative Supreme Court has reshaped this year's midterms
item.description:
Voters will pick the winners of next month’s midterm elections, but it is the conservative Supreme Court that has set the rules.

Long before early voting got underway to decide control of Congress, the court exerted an unusually profound impact on the election with a series of decisions that have reshaped redistricting, campaign finance regulations, efforts to identify noncitizen voters and mail voting – frequently in a way that has benefited Republicans.

Some of those decisions received little attention, like the court’s ruling this month that cleared the way for political parties – and particularly, Republicans – to pour millions more into television advertising in tight races. Others were more notable, like the 6-3 ruling in April that effectively gutted the Voting Rights Act’s power to protect minority voters, and prompted a new round of redistricting in Republican-led states.

Various rulings have exposed tensions among the justices that spilled into public view.

“The court has kind of blinded itself to the very deleterious effects of their rulings on how the political system works and has created a democracy that does not work as well as it should,” Justice Elena Kagan said at an event on Tuesday in a remarkably frank critique of the court’s actions.

Not all of the court’s decisions have backed the Republican position. Both conservative and liberal justices have been skeptical of efforts by President Donald Trump and his allies to alter mail ballot systems, for instance.

Despite Trump’s evidence-free claims of widespread voter fraud, the court in September notably rejected the president’s push to give the US Postal Service the unprecedented power to withhold potentially millions of mail ballots. In June, a 5-4 majority upheld state laws that permit mail ballots to be received a few days after Election Day. Even as he has fixated on alleged problems with mail voting, Trump himself has frequently cast a ballot by mail.

Trump nominated three of the court’s nine justices during his first term. None of the three dissented from the court’s USPS decision.

“Justice Kagan is wildly off base, as are claims that the Supreme Court’s recent record in election cases has favored Republicans,” Jason Snead, executive director of the Honest Elections Project, told CNN. “Her claims that the court has somehow undermined democracy are little more than political spin.”

If polls indicating that Democrats are poised for a victory next month are correct, then many of the Supreme Court’s recent election rulings may have only a negligible impact on the bottom line. But those following the long game say the impact of the Supreme Court’s decisions over the past year will be felt far beyond November.

“It’s critical to look beyond the partisan implications of the court’s decisions related to voting rights and to focus on how the court has undermined the very foundations of our multi-racial democracy,” said Samuel Spital, associate director-counsel of the NAACP Legal Defense Fund. “In a series of decisions over the last 13 years … a majority of unelected judges on the Supreme Court have dismantled the heart of the Voting Rights Act and put our multi-racial democracy in serious danger.”

What Snead described as “wildly off base,” Spital called “clear eyed.”

Kagan’s rare criticism of fellow justices

The timing of Kagan’s warning, just two weeks before the November 3 election, was notable.

“The people of America look around at this political system and think that all this money chasing all these political candidates is a nightmare,” Kagan said at the Catholic University law event last week. “And they’re right.”

Named to the Supreme Court by former President Barack Obama more than 16 years ago, Kagan is often viewed as the member of its three-justice liberal wing who is most receptive to compromise with her conservative colleagues. That often manifests in subtle ways, such as her decision not to join particularly pointed dissents written by the court’s other two liberals.

But when it comes to election disputes, Kagan has been unsparing both in her dissents and in public appearances.

Earlier this year, it was Kagan who wrote the dissent in the hugely important 6-3 decision gutting the Voting Rights Act, warning that the consequences would be “far-reaching and grave.” Asked last year about her favorite opinion she has authored, Kagan pointed to her dissent in another high-profile redistricting case from seven years ago.

Speaking at Princeton University in early 2025, Kagan used similarly stark terms to describe that case, in which the court’s 5-4 decision took federal courts out of the business of deciding challenges to partisan gerrymanders. In that decision written by Chief Justice John Roberts, the court concluded even extreme line drawing for political advantage is “beyond the reach of the federal courts.”

“What the court did in that case, I thought, was just a real mistake,” Kagan told her alma mater last year. “The foundation of our democracy is voting, and if the voting rights aren’t equal then how does a system of democracy work?”

Kagan noted then that she had written “a lot of voting rights dissents” and that it is “an area that I really care about.”

Mapmaking, noncitizens and money

The court’s most significant election decision this year came in April in a case called Louisiana v. Callais. With the conservatives aligned against the liberals, the court held that Louisiana’s decision to draw a second Black and Democratic district into the state’s overwhelmingly Republican delegation amounted to an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.

That decision set off a series of subsequent emergency rulings in which the court allowed both Louisiana and Alabama to quickly redraw their maps for this election in a way that targeted Democratic-held seats. Those decisions boosted Trump’s unprecedented mid-decade redistricting drive. When the dust settled, Republicans had gained an advantage in nine seats.

When Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, a liberal, suggested in May that the court was rolling over its “principles” in pursuit of influencing the November election, conservative Justice Samuel Alito called the insinuation “insulting.”

“What principle has the court violated?” Alito wrote. “The principle that we should never take any action that might unjustifiably be criticized as partisan?”

Not all of the redistricting decisions went Republicans’ way. The court three times rejected an effort by Missouri Republicans to draw a Democratic congressman out of his seat. And back in February, with no noted dissent, the court allowed California to use a Democrat-friendly map for this year’s election.

Some of the court’s other election decisions have drawn less fire but will nevertheless have an impact.

Over a dissent from the three liberal justices, the court last month allowed the Department of Homeland Security to provide citizenship verification to states based on a database critics say is riddled with errors. Trump has fixated on unfounded claims of widespread voting by noncitizens. The administration’s latest litigation on that front, challenging votes cast by some 20,000 Californians the administration believes could be noncitizens, is potentially on a path to Supreme Court review before the election.

And the Supreme Court on Thursday allowed New Hampshire officials to limit when voters may use a student ID to receive a ballot, agreeing that a lower court ruling that blocked enforcement of the policy was too close to Election Day.  A recent CNN poll found that Democrats enjoy a 31-point advantage over Republicans among younger adults.

The court last week backed a Republican effort to lower television campaign ad rates for political parties, rejecting an appeals court decision that would have subjected the Federal Communications Commission to faster judicial review of its decision making. In a related decision in June, the court erased limits on how much political parties could coordinate with federal candidates.

Together, the decisions likely incentivized a move this week by the Republican National Committee to unload over $50 million to help midterm candidates. Kagan blasted the decision in June, noting in dissent that it overruled a 2001 precedent and predicting it would flood more money into campaigns.

“For those who think there is too much of it in this country — for those who would prefer even more money to be pumped even more easily into politics despite the danger of corruption,” she wrote, “this overruling is for you.”

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com

This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/25/politics/supreme-court-midterm-rules

item.title: 特朗普宣布奥迪将斥资40亿美元在美建厂
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/特朗普宣布奥迪将斥资40亿美元在美建厂/a-79756218
item.description:
Midhat Fatimah
2026-10-25T16:06:24.259Z
特朗普将奥迪赴美建厂的决定归功于自己的关税政策。

（德国之声中文网）美国总统特朗普周六（10月24日）宣布，德国汽车制造商奥迪（Audi）将在美国佐治亚州投资40亿美元，兴建一座汽车组装厂。

特朗普在佐治亚州佩里市的一场竞选造势活动上表示，该工厂每年将生产20万辆SUV。

“想想看，一年20万辆汽车。这实在太惊人了”特朗普说。

特朗普将奥迪赴美建厂的决定归功于自己的关税政策。

中期选举临近 特朗普主打制造业议题

特朗普一直以来都在向外国和美国本土企业施压，要求将生产移至美国。其中主要手段之一就是对进口汽车广泛征收关税。

去年，特朗普的关税政策给奥迪造成了约14亿美元的损失。

美国中期选举即将到来之际，特朗普试图兑现自己“重振美国制造业”的承诺，希望借此为共和党候选人在这个关键摇摆州争取支持。

随着物价上涨以及伊朗战争持续，共和党人对于可能在11月3日的选举中遭受失利严阵以待。

奥迪怎么说？

大众汽车集团旗下的奥迪表示，新工厂预计将于明年动工，汽车生产则预计于2030年代初启动。

一名美国官员向路透社透露，该工厂预计将组装奥迪Q7、Q8以及Q9系列SUV车型。

奥迪还表示，这项投资预计将创造约4500个就业岗位。

item.title: 以色列将在大选日关闭所有约旦河西岸口岸
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/以色列将在大选日关闭所有约旦河西岸口岸/a-79756249
item.description:
德正
2026-10-25T15:51:19.389Z
在以色列对希伯伦市展开军事行动期间，被疏散的巴勒斯坦人的房屋上挂起以色列国旗

（德国之声中文网）以色列军方周日（10月25日）宣布，从当天起，巴勒斯坦人不得进入西岸的以色列社区工作；下周二的大选日全天关闭所有陆路口岸，禁止巴勒斯坦工人进出整个约旦河西岸地区。以色列将在下周二（10月27日）举行议会选举。

上周五，巴勒斯坦武装人员在希伯伦市（Hebron）附近发动袭击，造成两名以色列士兵丧生，另有三人受伤。两名袭击嫌疑人被击毙。以色列军方随后在约旦河西岸展开了军事行动。巴勒斯坦激进组织哈马斯对此次袭击表示赞赏，但并未宣称对此负责。以色列军队表示，已“逮捕了约40名嫌疑人，其中包括隶属于哈马斯和伊斯兰圣战组织（Islamic Jihad）的恐怖分子。”

希伯伦市长优素福·贾巴里（Yousef al-Jabari）向半岛电视台表示，自周五以色列发动突袭以来，已有约2200人流离失所。以色列国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）证实了这一数字。他在接受以色列公共广播公司（Kan）采访时称，在“我们彻底解决希伯伦境内所有与哈马斯相关的问题之前”，巴勒斯坦人“将不被允许返回”。

以色列总理内坦尼亚胡强调要让袭击者付出沉重代价，并称正计划开展一场以色列1967年首次占领约旦河西岸以来最大规模的行动。

（法新社、路透社）

item.title: 德语媒体：从仰慕到惋惜 – 中国人眼中的德国形象
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：从仰慕到惋惜 – 中国人眼中的德国形象/a-79734614
item.description:
null 媒体看中国
2026-10-22T14:27:40.929Z
德语媒体；从仰慕到惋惜 – 中国人眼中的德国形象

（德国之声中文网）《商报》驻华记者在其中国观感中写道，“德国制造”历来在中国享有极高的声誉。但现在说起德国汽车、德国铁路以及德国大学时，中国人原本由衷的敬佩，正在转变成嘲讽和惋惜。这篇题为《中国人心目里的德国形象正在发生变化》的文章写道：

“作为《商报》在上海的驻地记者，经常会有中国人向我打听德国的情况。多数情况下，他们的问题中会透露出真诚的关切：德国怎样才能重振活力？但有时也不乏同情、甚至略带居高临下的意味：德国怎么会落到今天这步光景？言外之意是指同中国的经济奇迹相比，德国的经济实力已经明显回落。两年前，这类问题会让我立即进入为德国辩护的模式。但我毕竟不是外交官，而是一名记者，让大家畅所欲言才是我应当做的。

不过，在中国的社媒里，有些说法实在是过于夸张。例如有人发出警告说，一定要远离法兰克福火车总站。有鉴于此，我的中文女老师就在落地法兰克福机场后直接乘火车去了科隆。事实上，科隆也比法兰克福好不到哪里去，只是较少引起中国社媒的关注罢了。

我并不是想说，中国人对德国的看法完全是错误的，而是要强调这种看法正在发生变化。在中国，德国的形象正在变坏，而这一切都可能会导致意想不到的后果。对那些长期以来对德国寄予厚望的中国家庭尤为如此：到德国企业就职，到中国的德语学校读书，以及申请德国高校进一步深造等等。

一旦对德国的兴趣降低，那么，德中双边的相互交流、相互了解以及个体体验对方国家的情况也有可能会随之减少。地缘政治层面上的对立以及各类间谍指控，都增加了相互交流的难度。不仅中国在德国的形象越来越负面，德国在中国的形象也日趋复杂，这无疑为双边合作增加了难度。”

《商报》驻华记者Martin Benninghoff写道，“德国制造”虽然仍在中国享有极高的声誉，但却早已失去了往日的光环。同五年前相比，上海街头的德国造汽车已经明显变少了：

“而要想恢复德国铁路准时准点的声誉，恐怕需要聘请最贵的广告公司，用二十年的时间想出各类绝妙的广告词。在小红书等中国社媒上，有关德铁晚点和站台乱象的段子随处可见，堪比我童年时代德国人取笑东弗里斯兰人的各类笑话。

2017年，一群正在德国游学的中国中学生。

这种变化也体现在中国年轻人的求学方向上。在德国的中国留学生数量已出现峰值回落的趋势：按照德国学术交流中心的数据，2019至2020冬季学期注册的中国学生为41353人，2024至2025冬季学期已经降至38989人。

当然，这一数据本身并不能说明德国形象的下滑，但却同我的切身感受高度吻合：即便是在德国影响相对较大的上海，年轻一代也不再像过去那样将德国列为他们的首选。”

 

”难以调和的中美贸易争端“

《法兰克福汇报》评论称，中美双方就贸易关系而展开的博弈中，双方虽然都不愿意让冲突升级，但也都不愿意做出实质性的让步：

“通过给贸易战‘停火状态’的短暂延期，华盛顿继续维持随时让冲突升级的高压态势，希望以此迫使北京在一月前做出更多让步。有鉴于此，今年年底对双方都是一场严峻考验。‘停火状态’延期至美国的中期选举和中共的五中全会之后，为双方提供了喘息之机。此外，在停火届满之前，亚太经合组织峰会以及G20峰会将分别在深圳和迈阿密举行。特朗普和习近平届时有可能会再度举行会晤。这一系列即将展开的政治议程可能促使中美政府都保持了克制，而没有进一步收紧贸易政策。

目前最有可能出现的情况是，华盛顿和北京在一月之前再度宣布延长‘停火状态’。双方都很清楚，冲突一旦升级，各自都要付出惨痛代价，但双方也都不愿意做出实质性的妥协。有鉴于此，双方达成内容广泛、且长期有效的协定，可能性微乎其微。中美双方在技术、供应链和产业政策领域已经形成了根深蒂固的矛盾。一月份过后，中美贸易关系恐怕仍将充满相互挑衅和局部性的相互反制。停火状态提供了喘息之机，但却无法为中美在技术和经济领域的争夺提供解决方案。”

摘编自其他媒体的内容，不代表德国之声的立场或观点。

item.title: 以色列大选前夕，以军为应对巴勒斯坦人枪击事件在约旦河西岸展开大规模军事行动
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

以色列大选前夕，以色列国防军（IDF）星期天（10月25日）在被占领的约旦河西岸展开大规模军事行动，以回应上周发生的一起恐怖枪击事件。那次袭击导致两名以色列士兵死亡，三人受伤。

以色列此次军事行动的重点地区是上周发生枪击事件的希伯伦市。行动导致数百名巴勒斯坦人流离失所，当地流动人员更是受到严格的限制。

根据以军采取的最新措施，大多数持有许可证的巴勒斯坦劳工在星期日和星期一将不被允许进入以色列在约旦河西岸的定居点。此外，通往以色列境内的过境点也将保持关闭，直至周二以色列选举结束后才会重新开放。

目前，以色列正处于一场竞争激烈的选举的最后冲刺阶段。这场选举在很大程度上被许多观察家视为对现任总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）过去三年执政期间领导能力及安全政策的一次“全民公投”。

此次选举是以色列自2023年10月7日遭哈马斯（Hamas）发动大规模突袭以来的首次大选。那次袭击给以色列军民造成严重损失，震惊了以色列全国，并使整个地区陷入动荡。此后，以色列在加沙地带与哈马斯开战，而战火同时也波及了黎巴嫩和伊朗境内的相关势力。

路透社报道说，2023年10月7日哈马斯袭击显现的以色列安全漏洞使内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团（Likud）的支持率大幅下滑。数月来的民意调查显示，内塔尼亚胡所主导的由右翼、极右翼及极端正统派政党组成的执政联盟，恐将失去议会多数席位。然而，他的主要竞争对手--中间派人士加迪·艾森科特（Gadi Eisenkot）--目前也尚无明确的胜选路径。随着下周二大选的临近，双方的竞争态势愈发胶着。

美联社援引以色列军方的消息说，以军本周末在约旦河西岸400多个不同地点展开了行动，逮捕了40名巴勒斯坦人。以色列军方声称这些人与哈马斯或“伊斯兰圣战组织”（Islamic Jihad）等武装团体有关联。军方称，相关行动星期天仍在继续。

以色列军方称，部队正在武装人员活动的区域进行搜查，并警告当地居民撤离希伯伦涉嫌武装人员所在的社区“代尔巴哈”（Deir Bahha）。在星期五的袭击事件发生后，以色列军方表示，他们在巴勒斯坦武装人员的车内发现了武器。军方认为，这些人原本可能计划袭击以色列平民，但在抵达一处检查站时被以军拦截，随后双方爆发了交火。

美联社援引希伯伦市市长优素福·祖海尔·贾巴里（Yousef Zuhair Al-Jabari）的话说，该市的所有出入口目前仍处于封闭状态。以军行动重点集中在“代尔巴哈”地区以及该市另一个名为“阿尔-贾尔达”（Al-Jalda）的区域。

“人们既无法进入这座城市，也无法离开。封锁影响了生活的方方面面，”贾巴里说。他补充道，封锁迫使许多商家关门，甚至导致一座清真寺也被迫关闭。

希伯伦市政府表示，此次以军行动迫使2600多人离开各自的住所。

“军方告诉我们，这一地区将被封锁12天。虽然现在说是12天，但也许两三天后他们就会撤离，”希伯伦居民沙迪·卡瓦斯米（Shadi al-Qawasmi）告诉美联社。他和家人因以军封锁而被迫流离失所。

“这可能是因为选举或其他政治原因。除了真主，谁也不知道真相，”卡瓦斯米说。

根据美联社记者的现场观察，此次以军行动迫使一些家庭不得不徒步离开希伯伦市。在一些军事关卡，人们将面粉袋和燃气罐从关卡处传递出去。一位老人推着坐在轮椅上的妻子，从关卡旁的一处缺口通过。另有一户人家试图穿过关卡，以便赴约就医。

希伯伦市政官员表示，在代尔巴哈及其周边地区，已有居住在近500套公寓里的家庭被迫流离失所。

约旦河西岸的暴力事件今年以来大幅增加，已经导致6名以色列人死亡。据巴勒斯坦卫生部统计，同期内有112名巴勒斯坦人死亡，其中包括被怀疑参与开枪袭击的巴勒斯坦武装人员。

星期五的恐怖枪击事件发生在以色列大选前夕，引起以色列选民的强烈愤慨。内塔尼亚胡在第一时间赶赴事发现场，并誓言要采取强有力的回应措施。

此次以色列大选攸关内塔尼亚胡的政治生命，因此使他面临强大的压力。美联社认为，内塔尼亚胡需要维持对巴勒斯坦袭击者的强硬姿态，从而在那些关注安全问题的以色列选民面前提升自己的形象。

路透社报道说，即使在长期作为利库德集团稳固据点的内盖夫沙漠偏远城镇迪莫纳（Dimona），一些感到失望的选民正挨家挨户地为内塔尼亚胡的主要竞争对手进行竞选拉票，希望能在下星期二举行的以色列大选中，让内塔尼亚胡下台。

“我们必须做出改变。‘比比’（Bibi，内塔尼亚胡的昵称）必须下台，”74岁的约西·阿萨亚格（Yossi Assayag）对路透社说。他表示，自己大半辈子都是利库德集团的支持者，但“‘比比’给以色列带来了灾难。”

退休人员鲁蒂·奥哈纳（Ruti Ohana）向路透社表示，自60多年前从北非移民到以色列，她一直都把票投给利库德集团。她认为，内塔尼亚胡远胜于他的竞争对手；而批评者因“10月7日事件”对他进行的指责，是不公平的。

“我绝不会背叛利库德集团，”她对路透社说。

根据以色列民主研究所（Israel Democracy Institute）下属维特比家庭民意与政策研究中心（Viterbi Family Center for Public Opinion and Policy Research）收集的数据，约有13%的以色列选民尚未决定如何投票。

不过路透社报道说，在2022年投票支持利库德集团的选民中，如今仅有55%的人表示会在星期二的选举中再次投票给该党。15%的人将转而支持反对内塔尼亚胡的政党阵营（其中8%支持“亚沙尔”党/Yashar），另有14%的人将投票给其他右翼政党。还有9%的人尚未决定投票给谁。

关键词: 
以色列
栏目: 
时事见解

新鲜看点

item.title: LIV Golf faces a make-or-break deadline — and only 4 players have signed on
item.description:
One way or another, LIV Golf is in its final days as originally created. The tour began life as a PGA Tour breakaway funded by Saudi Arabia's virtually limitless Public Investment Fund, but now is working to both line up financing and hold onto players in preparation for what league officials have termed "LIV 2.0." With a self-imposed go/no-go deadline nearing, several recent developments have complicated plans for a new version of the league. 

For players, LIV's chief drawing card was the paychecks with astounding numbers of zeroes. Stars, former stars and non-stars alike all cashed in during LIV's run, earning many millions more than they would have been able to on the PGA Tour or the Europe-based DP World Tour. But when Saudi Arabia cut off funding for LIV in April, the pipeline for those paychecks dried up, and now player after player has decided to take their chances elsewhere. 

The most notable defection came several weeks ago, when Jon Rahm decided he'd had enough of LIV. Rahm's jump to LIV in late 2023 was a seismic moment in golf history, a declaration that the league was capable of enticing even one of the world's best players. But after three years of absolute domination on LIV and underperformance in majors, Rahm opted to walk away from millions — perhaps even tens of millions — owed to him under his initial contract. Rahm's future plans aren't yet known, but the fact that he was willing to forgo the remainder of his contract is a stark statement on his belief in LIV 2.0. 

Several other notable players have followed Rahm out the door. In recent days, Ian Poulter announced he would be ending his LIV tenure, expressing gratitude on X for the opportunity:

Life update…✍🏼 pic.twitter.com/kdSQIOmxZ0

— Ian Poulter (@IanJamesPoulter) October 23, 2026

Rahm's Legion XIII teammate Tyrrell Hatton also announced he wouldn't be playing in LIV 2.0. Like Rahm, his next event will be the DP World Tour's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship in early November. Major winners Sergio Garcia and Louis Oosthuizen, among many others, have declared that they intend to pursue other opportunities outside LIV Golf. 

The defection of so many notable players — in name if not necessarily in current skill — makes the challenge of bringing LIV Golf 2.0 to light that much more difficult. Professional golf on an international scale is a star-driven system, and having notable names in the field is the fastest way to draw attention to an event. 

Accordingly, LIV's new investor, BC Partners Credit, had set a deadline of Sunday, Oct. 25, for players to commit to the league, though BC has the ability to move that deadline. LIV's own attorneys have suggested in recent bankruptcy hearings that the league would make a decision on its future existence by the end of this month. 

Several players aren't simply walking away from LIV, however; they're seeking what they claim they're still owed. On Sunday, The Athletic reported that more than 10 players, led by Masters champions Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson, are seeking more favorable severance deals from the Public Investment Fund. The unpaid terms of their contracts reportedly total more than $100 million. 

Johnson's attorney David Cornwell suggested that the players are reluctant to sign on with LIV 2.0 until the remaining obligations of LIV 1.0 reach a satisfactory conclusion. The Athletic reported that the PIF had offered the players two cents on the dollar for the remainder of those contracts, and Cornwell indicated that the PIF's decision to cut off funding for LIV ought to give other sports entities pause. 

"The PIF was an honorable business partner until what we regard as its abandonment of LIV golfers," Cornwell told The Athletic. "Professional sports leagues and their player unions in the United States, along with sports organizations worldwide, should take notice: the PIF's treatment of LIV golfers may signal how it will treat professional athletes in other sports. How you do one thing is usually how you do everything."

At the same time, court documents indicated that many LIV executives were paid hundreds of thousands or even millions of dollars in retention payments and bonuses prior to the league's bankruptcy filing this summer. While retention payments aren't uncommon during bankruptcy proceedings, the fact that LIV was paying significant amounts to executives while vendors went unpaid raised questions and opened up the league to external criticism. 

LIV and BC Partners have developed a plan that could bring in up to $300 million in financing for LIV 2.0, and players would hold a majority ownership stake in the new entity. However, as of the deadline date of Sunday only four players — Richard Bland, Ben Campbell, Brendan Steele and Cameron Tringale — had formally committed to the next iteration of the league. Bryson DeChambeau, a free agent who has been linked to the LIV restructuring in the last few months, has not formally committed to the next version of the league just yet. 

This article originally appeared on Yahoo Sports at https://sports.yahoo.com/golf/article/as-liv-golf-deadline-nears-players-are-departing-demanding-payment-171817228.html

item.description: 23日在法国近郊Yvelines 发生的反移民色彩枪击案和24日法国高度紧张的新一波社会运动是周末版法国《世界报》在头版头条重点凸出的内容。在国际版，该报以大版篇幅聚焦在中东动荡局势下即将启动的以色列大选以及以色列总理内塔尼亚胡对约旦河西岸发出的军事打击威胁。此外，也门反政府势力胡塞武装在也门境内的发展、意大利总理梅洛妮与各国保守派政党的关系等也是该报国际版关注的话题。美国中期选举临近，该报以特别报道德克萨斯州围绕大数据中心建设的争议。周末地缘政治专栏则聚焦如今寄居乌克兰首都的当年切尔诺贝利核电站事故幸存者对当前俄乌战争的感受。一名幸存者表示，当年的切尔诺贝利核电站事故是一个看不见的敌人，眼前的战争则发生在光天化日之下。本期《世界报》没有关于中国的特别报道。我们借本次节目时间，向大家介绍最新一期法国《快报》周刊关于2026年诺贝尔和平奖评选结果的争议的文章。文章认为围绕本届和平奖得主的争议进一步损害了该奖的声誉。
